Clicking the up/down buttons at the right end of the pivot X field to step by one, dragging up and down on them, picking a value from the right-click list, then clicking the Y field and typing a number
Size, coordinates, FPS, zoom, effect strength — every number field in the app supports the same three methods. Use whichever fits the moment.
Click and type
Click the field and type a number. You can also type arithmetic such as 256*2 (add, subtract, multiply, divide). Press Enter or click elsewhere to confirm.
Up/down buttons
Click the up/down buttons at the field's right end to step by one (Ctrl steps by 10). Drag up or down on them to change the value one step every 3 pixels (up increases, Shift is 10× slower, Ctrl steps by 10); when you hit the top or bottom of the screen, the cursor wraps around so you can keep dragging. While typing, each wheel notch changes the value by one step.
Right-click and pick
Right-click the field for a list of common values; the current value is marked with a dot. Recent: … in the list is the value before the last change, shared by fields of the same kind. Picking it lets you switch back and forth between two values; it is hidden when it equals the current value.
Details such as how expressions are calculated and the up/down buttons are in Number fields and menus.

The canvas pivot you set in Chickxel is written into the Unity .meta sprite pivot when you save. No adjusting in Unity — the anchor you want, like a character's feet or a weapon's grip, lines up the same in the game. Every layer also has its own pivot, so rotation, symmetry and transforms center on that layer's anchor.
Pick the Pivot tool (K)
Drag the anchor on the canvas, or use the 5×5 buttons and X/Y fields in the tool settings.
Choose the target
The pivot of the current layer selected in the timeline (normal layer, group or part) changes. Click the Canvas W×H text in the chip at the top left of the timeline to edit the canvas pivot used for export, and pick a Representative to make that layer's pivot the canvas pivot in every frame. Turn on From current frame on to give this frame and every later frame their own pivot.
Save to update Unity
Saving writes the canvas pivot (and each part's pivot for parts) into the .meta alongside the PNG sheet. Transform (Ctrl+T) starts rotating around the current layer's pivot.
Every Pivot tool setting is in Pivot tool.

pages.text:
Chickxel is a pixel art editor for games (especially Unity 2D). Frames, layers and tags (animations) are stored in a .chickxel project, and saving also produces a PNG sprite sheet and a Unity .meta. The app runs on its own; you don't need to install .NET or anything else.

Download the ZIP for Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel) or Linux (x64 or ARM64) and unzip it. You can also install by pasting one line into a terminal. Once installed, the app updates itself (see Updates).
Which file to download
OS Download (latest version) Run
Windows 10/11 Chickxel-windows-x64.zip Unzip and double-click Chickxel.exe
macOS 12 or later, Apple Silicon (M1 and later) Chickxel-macos-arm64.zip Unzip, move Chickxel.app to the Applications folder, then double-click it
macOS 12 or later, Intel Chickxel-macos-x64.zip Same as above
Linux, x64 (Intel or AMD) Chickxel-linux-x64.zip Unzip and run the Chickxel executable (chickxel.png next to it is the icon). If it doesn't start, turn on Allow executing file as program in the file's properties, or run chmod +x Chickxel in a terminal
Linux, ARM64 Chickxel-linux-arm64.zip Same as above
To see which chip your Mac has, open Apple menu → About This Mac. On Linux, run uname -m in a terminal: x86_64 means x64 and aarch64 means ARM64. Changes from earlier versions are listed on the releases page.
Installing from the terminal
macOS — paste the one-line command into Terminal to download the correct build for your chip, install it to /Applications/Chickxel.app and launch it. It detects the right chip even in a Rosetta terminal.
Linux — paste the same line into a terminal to download the build for your CPU, put it at ~/.local/share/Chickxel/Chickxel, add it to the applications menu (~/.local/share/applications/chickxel.desktop) with its icon, and launch it. It installs in your home folder, so sudo isn't needed.
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/1000Pro-1997/Chickxel/main/install.sh | sh
Windows — paste the one-line command into PowerShell to install in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Chickxel and create a Start menu shortcut. Because the browser does not download it, the 'Windows protected your PC' prompt does not appear.

Getting past the security warning

Windows "Windows protected your PC": More info → Run anyway.
macOS "unidentified developer": right-click → Open on Chickxel.app. If that doesn't work, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway.

When reporting a bug, including the following helps get it fixed quickly:
Version: shown in ③ Help > About Chickxel… at ⑥.
OS: Windows 10/11, your macOS version (Apple Silicon or Intel), or your Linux distribution and version (x64 or ARM64).
Steps: what you did, what happened, and what you expected.

To support development, use Support Chickxel development on the website, the Support development button at the top right of the in-app guide (F1), or ⑦ Buy the developer a coffee in ③ Help > About Chickxel…. The Website button in the same window opens the Chickxel website in the app's language.

pages.text:
A Chickxel account is used only to upload pictures to the chickxel.com gallery and to share effect and gradient assets. Drawing, saving and exporting don't need it. You sign in with a Google, GitHub or Discord account, and you can keep several accounts on one computer and switch between them. Sharing pictures and assets earns XP that raises your account level, shown as a level chip next to your name.
Signing in
The Chickxel Account window when signed out: an introduction and the Sign in with Google, GitHub and Discord buttons
Signed out: sign-in buttons
With a Chickxel account you upload pictures to the chickxel.com gallery (see Upload to gallery) and share effect and gradient assets (see Publish online). Open it with Help > Chickxel Account…. When signed out, it has sign-in buttons for Google, GitHub and Discord. Clicking one opens the chickxel.com sign-in page in your browser with that service chosen; when you finish, the browser says you can close it and the app window updates. While waiting there are Open Browser Again and Cancel Sign-in, and after 5 minutes you're asked to try again. Your account is created the first time you sign in.
Account window
The Chickxel Account window when signed in: picture, name, level chip and handle; the level and XP bar; the display name and handle fields with Save Profile; Open My Gallery Page, Sign Out and Add Another Account; and the list of other accounts signed in on this computer with their level chips
① Account · ② Level and XP · ③ Profile · ④ Gallery page, Sign Out, Add Another Account · ⑤ Other accounts signed in on this computer

② Level N with an info box on how to earn XP, a bar filled as far as you are toward the next level (in the chip's color), and below it your XP and the XP left to the next level (103 XP · 9 XP to the next level). Without level information from the server, this row isn't shown. The rules are under Account level below.
③ Profile: edit the display name and handle and click Save Profile. The handle is 3–32 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens and is used in your gallery address and as the author ID of assets. A handle someone else uses is reported as taken. After you have published an asset package the handle field is off and "The handle can't change after you publish an asset package." appears below it.
④ Open My Gallery Page opens your page on chickxel.com. Sign Out removes only this account from the list and doesn't switch to another one. Add Another Account… keeps the current account and shows the sign-in buttons (if the browser goes straight to an account that's already signed in, switch accounts on that service or use another service). Signing in again with the same account doesn't add a duplicate; it just renews that account.
⑤ Other accounts signed in on this computer: each other signed-in account with its picture, name, level chip and @handle, Switch and a sign-out icon button.
Account level
Sharing earns XP for your account, which raises its level. The chickxel.com server counts XP from what you currently have shared, likes, daily check-ins and the time the app is open; a withdrawn like removes its XP. Days are UTC days (they start at 09:00 in Korea).
How XP
Upload a picture to the gallery (up to 3 a day count) +10
Also share the editable .chickxel file with the picture +5
Publish a new asset package (one a day counts) +10
Upload a new version of a published package (once a day counts) +1
Each like from someone else on your art or assets +2
Like someone else's art or assets (3 a day count) +1
Daily check-in (your first app start or site visit of the day) +10
Each hour the app is open while you're signed in +1
Going from level L to the next takes 10 + 2 × (L − 1) XP (10, 12, 14 …), so level L starts at (L − 1) × (L + 8) XP (level 2 = 10 XP, 3 = 22 XP, 4 = 36 XP). There is no maximum level.
Level Level chip
1–4 Dim gray
5–9 Bronze
10–19 Silver
20–29 Gold
30–49 Cyan-to-purple crystal with a soft glow
50+ Rainbow with a glow
The level chip (Lv 7) follows the name on the account button, the account menu, the account window, the Upload to Gallery window, and next to authors in the Asset Manager's online list and details; chickxel.com shows a chip in the same tiers next to every name (with an XP bar and how to earn XP on your account page there). Hover over a chip to see the level and how to earn XP. Without a known level (an older server), there is no chip.
App time is counted every 10 minutes only while you're signed in; once an hour has filled up, the app reports it to the server for +1 XP (the server grants it at most once an hour per account, even with the app open on several computers). Time signed out isn't counted, and if the connection fails the app tries again 10 minutes later. When this XP raises your level, the status bar shows "Level up! Lv N".
The server grants the daily check-in once, the first time that day you start the app or visit chickxel.com while signed in. When the app receives it, the status bar shows "Daily check-in +10 XP"; if you already checked in that day, nothing is shown.
When a picture or asset package is deleted on chickxel.com (by you, by an admin, or through report handling), it disappears from the site, catalog and profile, the XP it earned (likes included) is removed, and its storage quota is returned right away. The server still keeps it, though, so an admin can restore it or delete it permanently.
Account button in the menu bar
The account button at the right end of the menu bar shows your round profile picture, name and level chip together when signed in (the picture is loaded once the account has been checked at startup; until then a person icon), otherwise a person icon and Sign In. With no saved accounts, clicking it opens the account window; otherwise it opens the account menu: your signed-in accounts (picture, name and @handle; the current one bold with a check; click another to switch), Add Another Account…, Manage Account… (Sign In… when signed out) and Sign Out. The gallery button right to the left of the account button is covered under Menu and top bar.
Gallery and asset uploads use the current account. An account whose sign-in the server ended is removed from the list; if you tried to switch to it, the account window opens with "This account's sign-in has ended and it was removed from the list. Sign in again.".
Wherever an account or author appears (the account button, menu and window, the Asset Manager and store, Effect Maker, Upload to Gallery, the author in the publish window, and the asset import confirmation), it's shown as a round profile picture and name together, followed by a level chip when the level is known (the chip is never cut off). Without a picture, or before it's loaded, a person icon is shown; hover over a cut-off name to see all of it.
When it connects and where it's stored
Chickxel contacts chickxel.com once in the background when it starts with a saved account (to check the current account, so the account button's picture and level and the account in the Upload to Gallery window show confirmed details from the start), when you first open the account menu, when you switch accounts, when you use the account window or uploads, and each time an hour of signed-in app time fills up. If it can't connect, the saved name is used as is (with a person icon on the account button); with no signed-in account it doesn't connect. Signed-in accounts are kept in community-session.bin in the settings folder (see Preferences).

Up/down buttons
The ③ up/down buttons at the right end of a number field change the value when you click them or drag up and down on them. Over the buttons the cursor turns into an up-down arrow. Dragging the number field itself doesn't change the value.
Action Result
Click the up/down button Steps up or down by one. Hold Ctrl (macOS ⌘) to step by 10.
Drag up/down on the buttons Dragging up increases and dragging down decreases the value, one step for every 3 pixels. Stops at the field's minimum and maximum.

Typing and expressions
Click a number field to start typing with the whole number selected. While typing, each wheel notch changes the value by one step (when not typing, the wheel scrolls the panel or list). Press Enter or click elsewhere (such as the canvas) to confirm.
Integer and decimal fields accept arithmetic such as 256*2. Press Enter or move the focus away and it becomes the result (512).
You can use +, -, *, /, parentheses and a minus sign; multiplication and division come first.
Integer fields drop the fraction toward zero (7/2 → 3). Decimal fields round to the number of decimals the field shows.
Invalid expressions, division by zero and values too large to hold are rejected, and the previous value stays.

Values show their unit (px, °, %, ms), and the current value is marked with a dot.

⑫ Order · ⑬ Name · ⑭ Mode · ⑮ Canvas size, anchor, delete originals · ⑯ Preview · ⑰ How it will look in the timeline
⑫ Order: the order you selected the files in at first. Drag rows or use the up/down buttons (top = first). Each row shows its size and frame count.

As layers One layer per file (first file on top)
As a group One group with a part per file (file sizes kept)
As skins One skin per file within a single group (skin name = file name). For tile or item variants swapped in the same spot

Deleted files (Delete, multiple allowed) and originals removed by merging go to the app's own trash without asking (including their PNG and .meta files).

⑱ List and preview · ⑲ Restore, Delete permanently, Empty · ⑳ Retention policy

You can select several items; permanent deletion and emptying ask for confirmation. An item isn't restored if a file with the same name is already in its original place.

Mouse wheel Zooms in or out around the point under the cursor (1–64×, the same steps as the minus and plus buttons on the top bar).
Ctrl (macOS ⌘)+wheel Changes the brush size instead of zooming.
Space+drag, middle-button drag Pans the view. The cursor becomes a hand while Space is held.
Ctrl+= · Ctrl+- · Ctrl+0 · Ctrl+1 Zoom in · zoom out · fit to window · actual size (1×). For the zoom box, see Menu and top bar.
Hold H Shows the previous frame while held, with "Viewing previous frame N" at the top left ("No previous frame" on the first frame). Release to go back.
Editing parts and groups
Canvas with the Gem part layer selected: the part at its own size, the rest semi-transparent
① Selected part · ② Rest of the frame, semi-transparent
Selecting a part layer shows ① only that part at its own size over the checkerboard, with ② the rest of the frame shown semi-transparently and the frame border dashed, so you can line things up. Selecting a group layer outlines each part, and you drag parts to arrange them (see Part (group) layers). A part's 9-slice border appears as dashed guides.
View overlays
Canvas view features: checkerboard, pixel and tile grids, symmetry guide, pivot, selection, onion skin
③ Checkerboard · ④ Pixel grid · ⑤ Tile grid · ⑥ Symmetry guide · ⑦ Pivot · ⑧ Selection · ⑨ Onion skin
These overlays are turned on and off with the view options and are never part of the image.
Overlay What it shows
③ Checkerboard Shows transparent areas as a gray checkerboard.
④ Pixel grid Pixel borders, shown only from the chosen zoom up.
⑤ Tile grid A line every tile (16×16 and light blue at first).
⑥ Symmetry guide The axis, shown only while symmetry drawing is on. It is the canvas center, or the pivot with Mirror around pivot. The brush cursor outline also appears faintly on the mirrored side.
⑦ Pivot The reference point for rotation and placement. With the pivot view on, the current layer's pivot (or the canvas pivot while you edit it via the canvas chip text) is the large marker (a circle with a cross: white in the Pivot tool, otherwise orange), and the current frame's pivots of the other visible layers and of the canvas are small dots with name labels. Parts are blue dots; normal layers, groups and the canvas are orange dots. Pivots at the same spot on screen share one label, and with four or more it lists the first two names followed by +N more. The canvas pivot is labeled Canvas; with a representative layer it isn't drawn separately, and that layer's name gets (Canvas) appended. With the pivot view off, the Pivot tool still shows the pivot it edits and the part pivots in the group view. In the Pivot tool, when an effect moves the pivot, the original spot is also shown with a dashed line.
⑧ Selection The dashed outline of the area chosen with a selection tool.
⑨ Onion skin Neighboring frames overlaid translucently.
Canvas in tiled mode, repeating the image
⑩ Tiled mode (the center is the tile you edit)
⑩ In tiled mode the center tile is the image you edit and the surrounding tiles are copies. Right-click the tiled mode button to set how many tiles repeat and whether the surroundings are dimmed.
Shown only while editing
When a hidden normal layer is selected, it shows semi-transparently on the canvas only, so you can keep drawing on it. It doesn't appear in the preview or exports.
While you use the Move tool, pixels pushed outside the canvas are shown dimmed (Move).
If the current layer is locked, "The current layer is locked and can't be drawn on" appears at the bottom left.
Brush tools outline the brush shape (square, circle, diamond) at the cursor.
Computing effects
Even with heavy effects on large images or many frames, the window doesn't freeze while effects compute. When a frame takes a while, the canvas gets a gray semi-transparent veil with the partial result showing underneath as it is computed, plus a loading icon and progress bar at the top right of the image area. The veil lifts all at once when the frame is done. If computing falls behind while you draw, new strokes appear right away without effects and the effects catch up afterwards. Light images update immediately without a veil.
To hide effects on the editing canvas, turn off the Effects button on the top bar.

Delete, reorder, move and copy the frames, layers, cels and effects selected in the timeline. Every edit is a single undo step.

To do this How
Delete Select, then Delete. Frames → delete frames, layers → delete layers (groups include their parts), cels → clear the image only, effects → delete the effects. You can't delete every frame or layer.
Reorder Drag an already selected frame header or layer name. Other columns/rows move aside to make room; Esc cancels. Parts move only within the same group.
Move or copy a block of cels ① Select several cells, then click inside and drag to move; hold Ctrl (or Alt) when dropping to copy. Pressing inside selected cels with Ctrl held starts a copy drag right away (copy cursor), even with a single cel selected; releasing without dragging adds or removes that cel like Ctrl+click. Both moves and copies keep links, as with linked copies below. Cels can't move to rows of a different size or type.
Copy and paste Ctrl+C or Ctrl+X, then Ctrl+V (or ② copy, cut, paste in the right-click menu). Cels overwrite the same shape with the clicked cell as top-left, frames are pasted as new frames after the selected frame, and layers as new layers above the original. Copies keep cel links; to copy only the images without links, use Ctrl+Shift+C (see Linked copies and images-only copies below). Cels picked one by one with Ctrl+click across gaps can't be copied or cut.
Bring in the previous frame's image Right-click an ③ empty cel → ④ "Copy image from previous frame"
Change duration or name Double-click a frame number = frame duration; double-click a layer name or F2 = rename in place (Enter confirms, Esc cancels)
New layers created by copying get their trailing number increased by 1 (item_1 → item_2, tile_009 → tile_010, or _1 if there's no number). Duplicate in the layer menu follows the same rule. Every edit is a single undo step.
Linked copies and images-only copies
Copying or cutting cels or frames in the timeline carries their link groups along. Paste into the same row (same layer and skin) and the pasted cels join the original group with the same color (blue stays blue, orange stays orange), so editing one changes them all. Paste into another row or document, or after the original group is gone (for example after a cut), and cels from the same group form a new group. The new group keeps the original color unless another group in that row already uses it, in which case it takes the first unused color. A single cel from a group is pasted without a link. If the paste target is a linked cel of another group, only that cel leaves its group. Dragging a block of cels to move or copy it follows the same rules. Every paste is one undo step.
Copy images only (no links) (Ctrl+Shift+C) copies only the images, without link groups, so pasted cels stand alone. Besides the Edit menu, it's in the cel right-click menu as Copy cels — images only, no links and in the frame header right-click menu as Copy frames — images only, no links. When the timeline doesn't have focus (for example on the canvas), it works like a regular copy.

runs.t: Left: Outline → Shadow · Right: Shadow → Outline

Effects are applied from the top of the effect list down, and each effect receives the image with the effects above it already applied. So Outline → Shadow casts the shadow of the outlined shape (left), while Shadow → Outline also draws the outline around the shadow (right). Change the order with the Up and Down buttons in the effects dialog or by dragging effect names in the timeline.
Each effect has an on/off checkbox, so you can turn it off for a while without deleting it. A turned-off effect stays in the list and isn't drawn.
Effects that draw after all other effects, such as Afterimage, are drawn last regardless of their place in the list.

(for example, a gradient on the outline only).
Normal layers and parts apply effects to their own cels;
groups apply them to the combined shape of their parts
. For example, a group outline is drawn as one line around the whole character, while outlines on each part also draw lines where the parts meet.

Layer effects are non-destructive: they are applied only when the layer is displayed, without changing cel pixels. Stack as many as you like on each layer — from looks such as outlines and shadows to animated touches such as hit flashes, shakes and explosions — and turn them off, change or remove them at any time. They apply automatically to anything you draw later, and every effect is drawn per pixel (no blur or anti-aliasing).
Use them to put an outline or shadow around a whole character at once, to add a flash or blink on just a few frames (such as the moment of a hit), to make a recolored version of the same drawing (Palette swap), or to put text on the image (Text). When you need to edit the result as pixels, apply the effect permanently.

The same chick with an outline and a shadow applied in two different orders
Left: Outline → Shadow · Right: Shadow → Outline
Effects are applied from the top of the effect list down, and each effect receives the image with the effects above it already applied. So Outline → Shadow casts the shadow of the outlined shape (left), while Shadow → Outline also draws the outline around the shadow (right). Change the order with the Up and Down buttons in the effects dialog or by dragging effect names in the timeline.
Each effect has an on/off checkbox, so you can turn it off for a while without deleting it. A turned-off effect stays in the list and isn't drawn.
Effects that draw after all other effects, such as Afterimage, are drawn last regardless of their place in the list.
To make an effect draw from only the pixels drawn by the effect above it, turn on clipping (for example, a gradient on the outline only).
Layers, parts and groups
Normal layers and parts apply effects to their own cels; groups apply them to the combined shape of their parts. For example, a group outline is drawn as one line around the whole character, while outlines on each part also draw lines where the parts meet.
Applying permanently
Apply effect permanently bakes the effect into the cel pixels and removes it from the list; you can then edit the result like any drawing. Enabled effects above the selected one are baked too, so the result looks exactly as before. Use the Apply permanently button in the effects dialog or the right-click menu of a timeline effect box; while baking, a Baking effects progress overlay (percentage) appears.
Group effects and effects on locked layers can't be applied permanently (for a group, apply them to the parts).
Duplicating a layer also copies its effects, and Merge down bakes the upper layer's effects.
Where effects show
The canvas shows effects when Show effects on canvas is enabled; preview, frame sheets and part atlases apply effects too. Normal, group and part thumbnails in the timeline show editable art without effects (except text-effect cels with no painted pixels). The selected part view shows its own and its group's effects when enabled, or its plain source cel when disabled.
The part atlas includes only the part's own effects; spreading effects such as outlines or shadows make the sprite wider by that amount (the pivot is shifted so it points at the same spot).
Effects this version doesn't know
Effects this version doesn't know (for example, ones added in a newer Chickxel) are not thrown away. Opening such a project shows the notice "Unknown effect (type ID) on layer "…" is not drawn; it is kept as is when you save.", and the effect list shows a dimmed Unknown effect · type ID row (its checkbox is locked). Selecting it only explains that it can't be drawn or edited and Apply permanently is off, but you can still reorder or delete it. Its timeline effect row is gray.

Four chicks: no effect, default outline, 8-direction outline, outline shaded from neighbors
From left: no effect · Outline default (black, 1 px) · 8 directions (incl. corners) · Shade from neighbors
The default outline only looks at the neighbors above, below, left and right, so corners stay open and look stepped. 8 directions (incl. corners) also fills diagonal neighbors for a thicker border. Shade from neighbors paints the line with a darker version of the touching color, for a softer border than black (right — dark orange next to the feet).
Three chicks: no effect, semi-transparent shadow, 50% dither shadow
From left: no effect · Shadow X/Y 2 (Dither None (semi-transparent)) · the same shadow with Dither 50% (checkerboard)
Without dither, the background shows through according to the shadow color's transparency (semi-transparent black by default). With dither the shadow becomes a checkerboard-like dot pattern instead of semi-transparency, for a pixel-art shadow (25% and 75% make the dots sparser or denser).

Under each effect's own settings come the same common rows. They decide when the effect applies (effect range), how fast it moves (speed and repeat), what happens after the range ends (Cels after the range), whether later effects' centers follow it (Later effects) and whether OK expands the canvas (On OK). Effect range
The effect range is the frames an effect applies to: All frames (including frames added later) or a start–end frame. Animated effects start on the first frame of the range and finish on the last, so a longer range makes the same motion slower and a shorter one faster.

Insert it into other layers or projects in one go from the Presets tab of the effects dialog; with parameters, a few values adjust the whole bundle. Presets are used on this computer and shared as asset files, but not published online — to publish an effect, make it a script effect in the Effect Maker.
Use them to give every character the same outline + shadow combination, to insert a frequently used combo such as hit flash + shake in one go, or to change the color of several effects with a single value (parameters).
Basic workflow
Build the effect list you want in the effects dialog.
Click Save Current Effects as Preset at the top of the Presets tab, choose a name and preview chick, and save.
In the effects dialog of another layer or project, double-click the preset on the Presets tab or drag it into the effect list.
To adjust the whole bundle with a few values, define parameters (see Setting parameters below).
Presets tab
Presets tab of the effects dialog: the Save Current Effects as Preset button, two of my preset tiles, and a received preset tile with its tooltip
① Save Current Effects as Preset · ② My presets · ③ Received preset
Build an effect list in the effects dialog and click ① Save Current Effects as Preset to open the save window; saving makes it ② one of your presets. ③ Received presets (downloaded with the Asset Manager or imported from asset files) show on the same tab (the tooltip names the Store entry, or the author). Double-click a tile or drag it into the effect list. Inserted presets are copied by value, so they stay in the project and remain editable even if you change or delete the original preset.
Tile right-click menu: your presets have Rename, Edit parameters, Delete and Show in Asset Manager; received presets only have Show in Asset Manager. To change a received preset, make your own copy with Copy to My Assets in the Asset Manager.
Saving a preset
Save preset window: the preset name field and the numbered preview chick picker
④ Preset name · ⑤ Preview chick
Enter ④ a name (it starts as the first effect's name). If one of your presets already has that name, you are asked whether to overwrite it. Under ⑤ Preview chick, pick None in the first slot or one of 20 numbered chicks (chick 1 by default; you can pick again when overwriting). When you export the preset as an asset file, a preview of the effects on this chick (animated for moving effects) is made automatically. With None, the effects are drawn on an empty transparent canvas of the default chick size without a chick (for effects that draw on their own, such as rain or snow).
Setting parameters
Preset parameters window: parameter list with Add and Remove on the left; name, linked settings and default on the right
⑥ Parameter list with Add and Remove · ⑦ Name · ⑧ Linked settings · ⑨ Default (and range for integers)
A parameter ties one setting from each of several effects in the preset to a single value. For example, link the outline color and the shadow color to a "Color" parameter, and after inserting you change both with one value.
Right-click one of your presets on the Presets tab and choose Edit parameters (your preset's details in the Asset Manager have the same button).
Click Add to create a parameter in the ⑥ list and give it a ⑦ Name.
Under ⑧ Linked settings, check the settings this value changes together. Each preset effect lists the settings it can expose as "number. effect name · setting key (kind)". The first link sets the parameter's kind and default (that setting's current value); settings of another kind and settings already linked to another parameter are disabled.
Depending on the kind, set ⑨ the Default, the Range for integers or the Choices for choices, then click OK.
Invalid links or ranges are listed as problems at the bottom of the window, and OK stays off until they are fixed. The preset details in the Asset Manager list the number of parameters with their names and kinds.
Using a parameter preset
Effects dialog: a parameter preset as a single row in the effect list, with only the preset name, source and parameters in the settings
⑩ Preset group row · ⑪ Parameters · ⑫ Show effects and Ungroup
⑩ A preset with parameters appears in the effect list as one row, "preset name · preset, N effects" (with an expand arrow and a group icon).
⑪ Selecting that row shows only the preset name, source and parameters in the settings; changing a value updates every linked effect setting together.
⑫ Show effects lists the effects inside under the group row so you can edit them one by one, and Hide effects folds them again. Ungroup turns them into ordinary effects with their current values (the parameters go away).
A collapsed group moves, drags, deletes and applies permanently as one unit.

pages.text:
A script effect is a layer effect written in JavaScript. The official effects such as Outline and Shadow, effects from the Store and effects you make yourself are all script effects, and you add and edit them like any other layer effect. The source is saved inside the project file, so it draws the same on another computer, and it runs in an isolated engine with no file or network access, within time, statement and memory limits per frame.
This page covers using script effects (settings, editing the source, allowing them to run, errors). New effects are made and published in the Effect Maker, and the names and rules you can use in a source are in Script API.
In the effects dialog
Effects dialog with a script effect selected: my script effect tile at the end of the Effects tab, and the name, status line, edit buttons, Save as asset and settings in the settings panel

④ Save as asset: saves this source as one of your script effects (an asset) to reuse from the Effects tab and the Asset Manager and to edit in the Effect Maker. Only scripts allowed to run can be saved, and saving the same source twice keeps one copy.

Sources you set to Don't run when opening a project stay blocked until you allow them or install them again.
When a script can't draw
When a script effect can't draw, a warning icon appears at the end of its effect list row and on its timeline effect row (at the right end of the name cell and of the effect box); hover the icon in the effect list for the reason.
Status Cause and fix
Missing source The project doesn't contain the source. Open the same JS file (Open JS file… in the settings) to draw it again.
Not allowed The script isn't allowed to run. Click Allow to run in the settings.
Source error The source has syntax or declaration errors. Fix them in the editor.
Failed A frame went over the limits (2 seconds, 50 million statements and 256 MB of allocations, plus 100 µs, 500 statements and 6 KB per pixel of the image) or the script threw an error. Only this effect is skipped on that frame.
Stopped It failed 3 times in a row, so computing stopped. Fix it, then click Run again in the settings or turn the effect off and on.
Script effect assets
Tiles of received and own script effects on the Effects tab have a code icon (two angle brackets) at the top right (official effects don't). The tooltip shows the source's description and, for received effects, the Store name (or the author), and says so when the script isn't allowed to run. Right-click one of your script tiles for Edit in Effect Maker, Delete and Show in Asset Manager; received effects only have Show in Asset Manager (the name comes from the declaration in the source).
When you save a preset containing script effects or export it as an asset file, the source goes with it, so it draws the same on another computer.
In the Asset Manager, script effects have the kind Script effect and show under the Effects filter; their details list the author, source hash, Script run (allowed / not allowed) and the number and names of settings. Scripts not yet allowed get an orange note. Edit in Effect Maker in the details of your own script effect closes the Asset Manager and opens it in the Effect Maker. For a received script effect, Copy to My Assets makes your own editable copy.

pages.text:
This page is for writing or editing a script effect's source yourself. It covers the shape of a source (declaration), setting types, the img and ctx used in render and the global helpers, the fast path and limits, reading other layers and frames, and randomness and gradient colors. The same rules and full list are also in the Effect Maker's Rules window and the code editor's autocompletion.
Script API: declaration
One source is one effect. Call effect({ … }) exactly once at the top and keep only const values and function declarations besides it (no import or export). render(img, ctx, s) is called for every frame, changes img.data in place and returns nothing. The same image, frame and settings must always give the same result, so Date, Math.random, eval/Function, files, network, timers and console aren't available (use ctx.hash and ctx.random for randomness). The same rules and the full list are in the Effect Maker's Rules window.
Below is the skeleton that New script in the Effect Maker starts from (comments removed). It declares one setting (Strength), and render moves the red of every non-transparent pixel toward 255 by that strength.
effect({
  name: "New effect",
  language: "en",
  settings: [
    { key: "strength", label: "Strength", type: "int", min: 0, max: 100, default: 50 },
  ],
  render(img, ctx, s) {
    const d = img.data, k = s.strength / 100;
    for (let i = 0; i < d.length; i += 4) {
      if (d[i + 3] === 0) continue;
      d[i] = lerp(d[i], 255, k);
    }
  },
});
Name Meaning
name Effect name (1–100 characters, required), shown in the effect list and assets
description Short description (up to 200 characters). The Effect Maker's description field and the initial short description when you publish
author Author name (shown in the run confirmation window)
language Language code of the declared name, description and setting labels ("ko", "en", "zh-Hans" …). In that UI language the declared values are shown
translations Name, description and labels in other languages, { name, description, labels } (labels: setting key → label, "key.choiceValue" → choice label). The one for the UI language is shown in the effects dialog, the layer effect list and the Asset Manager
tags Up to 8 lowercase English tags (letters, digits, hyphens). Used as the tags when you publish
settings List of settings { key, label, type, min, max, step, default, choices, alpha, widget, pair, when } (table below). when shows a row only when an earlier choice/bool matches; even hidden values are read as s.key in render
render(img, ctx, s) Called for every frame; changes img.data in place. The same input must always give the same result
animated · motion · easing animated: true for effects that change with progress (adds speed and repeat settings). motion: false hides speed and repeat (for example blinking timed in frames). easing is the initial easing of a newly added effect ("Linear", "EaseIn", "EaseOut", "EaseInOut")
padding Margin the effect adds outside the image: [left, top, right, bottom] or padding(s, width, height) { … }
area · radius "global" (default, once per frame with the whole image) or "local" (per tile, with radius px around it)
repeat · repeatCount · movePivot Animated effect defaults: Once/Loop/PingPong (default Once) · repeat count 1–8 (default 1) · whether later effects' centers move with the image (default true, false turns it off)
expandCanvas Initial value of On OK [Expand canvas] when the effect is newly added from the effects dialog or by AI (default true). With false it is added with canvas expansion off (for effects that rise above the image, such as a campfire; effects already added keep their value). Anything but true/false is a declaration error
deferred When true, draws after all other effects regardless of its place in the list (like Afterimage). Only such effects get ctx.renderedFrameSource
previewChick · previewEndChick Preview chick ID (default "original") and end chick ID. In number order 1–20: original, painter, pencil, palette, easel, paint-bucket, designer, heart-canvas, cursor, hatch, knight, wizard, archer, ninja, pirate, astronaut, viking, king, gamer, healer (anything but lowercase letters, digits and hyphens is a declaration error). previewChick: "none" draws the preview on an empty transparent canvas of the default chick size without a chick (for effects that draw on their own, such as rain or snow; the check always uses the 20 sample chicks)
previewFrames Number of frames in the preview, the check and the published preview (2–20, default 10)
previewMotion Preview chick movement: "none" (default), "right", "left", "up", "down" (1 px per frame) or one [x, y] per frame (−32 to 32; later frames keep the last one). Only previews move
previewPivot · previewEndOffset · previewEndPivot Preview position and pivot (each [x, y] in px, right and down are +, −64 to 64, 0 when omitted): offset of each frame's pivot (ctx.pivot) from its default place, the chick's center (every frame but the last when there is an end chick) · offset of the end chick from its place · offset of the last frame's (the end chick's) pivot. The two end values are used only with previewEndChick. Only previews change
Script API: setting types
type Field in the effects dialog s.key value
int · number Slider and number field (min, max, step; number shows the digits of step). widget: "angle" = angle dial, widget: "point" + pair = X/Y point picker. Key seed adds a dice button Number
bool Checkbox labeled with the setting name true / false
color Color swatch with solid/gradient (opaque only with alpha: false). default like "#ff8800" { r, g, b, a } — gradients via ctx.color
choice Drop-down list (choices: [{ value, label }]) The chosen value
colorList Color list (min, max = item count; default 0–16, up to 64) [{ r, g, b, a }, …] — item colors via ctx.colorAt
colorPairs From → to color pair list (default [{ from, to }, …]) [{ from, to }, …] — ctx.pairColor
layer Layer picker. default is a layer name like "ground" (up to 64 characters; none chosen when omitted). min, max, step, choices, alpha and widget aren't allowed The chosen layer name ("" when none) — read the layer with ctx.layer(key)
when Show the setting only when an earlier choice/bool setting matches. Hidden values remain stored and accessible to render when: { facing: "rotate" } · when: { facing: ["rotate", "flip"] } · when: { closePath: true }
A script setting with when: { facing: "rotate" } or when: { facing: ["rotate", "flip"] } appears only when an earlier choice setting has that value. when: { closePath: true } tests an earlier bool. All conditions must match; if a dependency is hidden, its dependents are hidden too. Changes show or hide rows immediately in the effects dialog, tool dock and Effect Maker preview. Hidden values remain saved and accessible as s.key in render(img, ctx, s). Referring to a missing/later setting, a non-choice/non-bool setting or a nonexistent choice value is a declaration error. Autocompletion suggests when as well.
Script API: img, ctx and globals
Name Meaning
img.width · img.height · img.data Size of the padded image and its RGBA numbers (length = width × height × 4; the red of pixel (x, y) is at (y * img.width + x) * 4; written values are rounded to 0–255)
img.blank(w, h) · img.blendOver(src, x, y) Makes an empty (transparent) image · alpha-blends src at (x, y)
ctx.progress · ctx.phase · ctx.t Progress 0–1 within the effect range: progress includes loop and easing (animated effects usually use it), phase only the loop, t neither
ctx.frame · ctx.step · ctx.span Frame being drawn (from 0) · frames since the first frame of the range · range length − 1
ctx.rangeStart · ctx.rangeEnd · ctx.frameTag First and last frame of the effect range (0 and the last frame in the Effect Maker preview) · name of the tag containing this frame ("" when none or in previews)
ctx.source · ctx.pivot · ctx.center Where the original sits in the padded image { x, y, w, h } · pivot { x, y } · center { x, y } of the source (canvas, or the part rectangle) — always the center, unlike the pivot
ctx.movePivot(dx, dy) Report image displacement in pixels to this frame's pivot, rendering bounds and later effects. Fractions allowed; calls accumulate; no return value; works on the fast path
ctx.slice 9-slice border { left, top, right, bottom } (project border for the canvas, part border for parts). null when there is none, it doesn't fit, or outside a project
ctx.color(키, x, y, 범위?) · ctx.colorAt(키, i, x, y, 범위?) · ctx.pairColor(키, i, "from"|"to", x, y, 범위?) Color { r, g, b, a } at (x, y) of a color setting, color list item or pair side. The solid color, or for gradients sampled like the official effects over the opaque bounds of the image before the effect (or the given bounds { x, y, w, h })
ctx.hasGradient(…) Whether a color slot has a gradient: "key", "key[0]", "key[0].from", or (listKey, index, "from"|"to")
ctx.hash(x, y, seed, salt?) · ctx.random(seed) A number from 0 up to 1 fixed by position, seed and purpose (salt), or by frame and seed (always the same)
ctx.bayer2(x, y) · ctx.bayer4(x, y) 2×2 (0–3) and 4×4 (0–15) ordered-dither thresholds
ctx.frameSource(i) The source of frame i before effects (same size). null when missing or a different size
ctx.renderedFrameSource(i) Deferred effects only: frame i with this layer's other effects applied, { image, offsetX, offsetY }
ctx.matchPixels(a, b, mode?) Pairs the opaque pixels of two images (sizes may differ) as { count, data } ([ax, ay, bx, by] per pair; pixels of the smaller side are reused). Mode "color" orders by brightness first (default: by position). null when a or b is null
ctx.layer(키) · ctx.layerWithEffects(키) · ctx.layerEffects(키) The layer chosen in a layer setting on this frame (without / with its effects, aligned to img) and the names of its enabled effects. null or an empty array when there is none
lerp · hsvToRgb · rgbToHsv · rgbToOklab · oklabToRgb · Math Global helpers: lerp(a, b, t), HSV and OKLab conversion (the app's own OKLab math), Math (no Math.random). Typed arrays: Float64Array, Int32Array, Uint8Array
Scripts that move their image must report per-frame pixel displacement with ctx.movePivot(dx, dy). Arguments are pixels in image coordinate directions (fractions allowed), repeated calls add up, and nothing is returned; it runs on the fast execution path too. Later effects' pivots, part pivot markers, automatic render-padding growth and post-range held positions use the report. Existing scripts such as Follow path or Gravity throw that do not report motion need a call at the actual movement calculation in Edit script. Declaration keys: repeat is Once/Loop/PingPong (default Once), repeatCount is 1–8 (default 1), and movePivot defaults to true; false disables following-center motion on newly added effects. AI inserts also use these defaults.
Fast path and limits
A source runs on the fast path or on Jint. When render uses only numbers, booleans, loops, if, Math, lerp, helper functions taking numbers and img.data, the app converts and compiles it (fast path); strings, objects, arrays, closures, recursion and the like run on Jint with the same result, only slower. The Effect Maker status shows which path is used and why (what on which line).
These run on the fast path too: ctx.center, ctx.frameSource, ctx.matchPixels, ctx.color/ctx.colorAt/ctx.pairColor with the key written literally, and ctx.layer/ctx.layerWithEffects (including the usual null checks if (!g), g ? … : …, g === null). ctx.slice, ctx.layerEffects and reading a layer setting value s.key run on Jint.
Limits per frame: 2 seconds, 50 million statements, 256 MB of allocations and call depth 256, plus 100 µs, 500 statements and 6 KB per pixel of the image (bigger images get more; the fast path has no image size cap). Over a limit the effect is skipped on that frame, and after 3 failures in a row it stops. Keep the work proportional to the pixel count (no big loop per pixel).
Reading other layers
To read another layer or draw in relation to it, add a layer setting (for example { key: "ground", label: "Ground", type: "layer", default: "ground" }) so the user picks the layer, then read it in render with ctx.layer("ground") (without effects), ctx.layerWithEffects("ground") (with this frame's effects) or ctx.layerEffects("ground") (names of enabled effects). There is no way to read a layer by position or by a name written in the code.
It returns the nearest layer with the chosen name (excluding this layer and the group containing it; hidden layers count), aligned to img (same size and position, transparent outside, without layer opacity). When nothing is chosen, the layer or cel doesn't exist, the key isn't a layer setting or there is no project, it returns null (ctx.layerEffects: an empty array), so always check for null. ctx.layerWithEffects skips that layer's effects that read other layers with effects, so layers reading each other never loop.
Changing the pixels, effects, name or order of the layer being read, or the 9-slice border, redraws the effect right away on the canvas, the timeline, the effects dialog preview and exports. In the Effect Maker the layer is picked from the preview scene, and publishing always adds the layer-reference tag.
Effects that use several frames (transform)
ctx.frameSource(i) reads another frame before effects. Effects using it also draw on frames without a cel, so put pictures only on the first and last frames and apply a transform effect over that range to fill the frames in between.
Transform example: get a = ctx.frameSource(ctx.rangeStart), b = ctx.frameSource(ctx.rangeEnd) and m = ctx.matchPixels(a, b), clear img.data, then draw each pair moving from (ax, ay) to (bx, by) and blending its color with ctx.progress. Preview and check it before saving with the Effect Maker's End chick; publishing always adds the frame-reference tag. ctx.frameTag lets an effect draw differently per frame tag.
Randomness and gradient colors
Randomness comes from a seed: add { key: "seed", label: "Seed", type: "int", min: 0, max: 9999, default: 1 } to get the dice button in the effects dialog, and use ctx.hash(x, y, s.seed, salt) and ctx.random(s.seed) so each seed gives a different look and the same seed always the same one. Give each random value its own salt (e.g. 0 = direction, 1 = speed) and feed values that don't change per frame, such as a piece number, so pieces follow the same path in every frame.
Users can switch color settings to gradients. Instead of reading s.key once, pick the color for each pixel you write with ctx.color("key", x, y) (lists: ctx.colorAt, pairs: ctx.pairColor) so gradients are followed. Pass bounds { x, y, w, h } as the last argument when the default area doesn't fit, and use s.key only when the effect really needs a single color. The Effect Maker's check points out color settings that draw in a single color only.

㉘ The model list left of Send is the same list as the model field in the AI chat header. Changing it shows "Model: … — applies from the next message." and the conversation continues. The chosen AI and model are saved right away and kept the next time; the AI chat shares the same setting (the last choice wins).

The AI panel can look at the open drawing, layers, effects and references but can't change them (the app blocks that with a separate access key for the panel). pages.text:
The Effect Maker is the window for creating and editing script effects, previewing them on sample chicks, checking them and publishing them to the Store. One source is one effect, and its title, description, tags and preview chick live in the source's declaration too, so one source file is the same effect on any computer. Effect presets (bundles of several effects) aren't made here.
Open it with AI > Effect Maker… (sparkles icon, at the bottom of the AI menu). The AI panel on the right is open from the start (close and reopen it with the AI button). Edit in Effect Maker on your script tile in the effects dialog (right-click) or in your script effect's details in the Asset Manager opens that effect.
Basic workflow
Start from the skeleton with New script, or pick one of your effects in the list.
Edit the source yourself, describe the effect in the AI panel, or copy the rules window to another AI and paste its answer.
Check the look with the preview and the preview setting values, then Save (Ctrl+S). It is now available on the Effects tab of the effects dialog.
To share it, run Check on the 20 sample chicks and click Upload….
Window layout
Effect Maker window: my effects list and info on the left, code editor and preview setting values in the middle, chick preview and frame strip on the right, Save, Insert, status, Check and Upload buttons at the bottom
① My effects list · ② New script and Open JS file · ③ Info · ④ Rules · ⑤ Code editor · ⑥ Preview setting values · ⑦ AI · ⑧ Preview and frame strip · ⑨ Preview chick and end chick · ⑩ Play, show without effect, frames, motion, position and pivot · ⑪ Save and Insert into layer · ⑫ Status button · ⑬ Check, Upload, Close
① My effects: script effects made on this computer or published with your account (unchanged copies of received effects are left out). Turn on Show all at the top right to also see those copies and received script effects (package icon). Effects linked to the Store show the author's profile picture (a person icon when there is none) and name next to their name; effects made only on this computer show just a code icon and the name. Right-click: Delete (your own only) and Show in Asset Manager.
② New script starts from a short skeleton (a name in the UI language, one "Strength" setting and a loop over the pixels); Open JS file… opens a .js file's source as a new, unsaved effect.
③ Info: the header shows the developer of the open effect on the right (the author's profile picture and name for effects published to the Store, a person icon and 'Made on this computer' for effects made on this computer). Below it are Title (1–100 characters), Description (up to 200) and Tags. Editing them changes name, description and tags in the declaration, and editing the source updates the fields. The language being edited always shows next to the field names: when the UI language differs from the declared language, the translation for the UI language is shown and edited (empty if there is none; the dim text is the base value). Older scripts without language show the UI-language translation if there is one, else the declared values (Base (language not set)). Type tags like #neon and press Space, Enter or a comma to add a chip (X removes it, Backspace in the empty field removes the last one; up to 8, lowercase English letters, digits and hyphens).
③ Languages below opens a window for the title, description and setting labels in each language (add or remove languages, type another language code, empty fields show the source values, languages with text are green with a check mark — translations in the declaration). Base language at the top is the language of the declared title and description; without language it is guessed from the letters (Hangul → Korean, kana → Japanese, Han → Simplified Chinese, Cyrillic → Russian, Thai → Thai, Latin → English). OK writes it into the source as language. The name matching the app's UI language is shown in the effects dialog, the layer effect list and the Asset Manager.
④ Rules (right of the Info header, book icon) shows the rules for writing an effect and the API (see Rules window below).
⑤ The code editor is the same as the script editor of the effects dialog (syntax colors, autocompletion, error underlines — see Script effects). Undo (Ctrl+Z) works in the editor.
⑥ Preview setting values: pick effect-specific settings, animated easing/repeat/repeat count and motion-reporting pivot movement in the same order as the Effects dialog and right dock. Values affect the preview and Insert into layer; Reset restores source defaults, and Set as default writes the currently chosen values as defaults.
⑦ AI (right of the Preview header, sparkles icon) opens and closes the AI panel on the right of the window (see AI panel below).
⑧ The preview is the same image that is made when you publish: the effect on the chosen chick over as many frames as the frame count (0.1 s each). It redraws shortly after you edit the source or settings. The frame strip below shows each frame with its number; click one to pause on it (while playing, the highlight follows).
⑨ Preview chick: pick None in the first slot or one of 20 chicks by picture and number (changes previewChick in the source; with errors in the source you are asked to fix them first). With None ("none"), the preview and the published preview draw the effect on an empty transparent canvas of the default chick size (at the same place in the preview scene, if there is one) without a chick. Use it for effects that draw on their own, such as rain or snow. End chick is for transform effects (below).
⑩ Play/pause icon button, Show without effect (eye-off toggle), Frames (2–20, previewFrames in the source — used by the preview, the check and the published preview; a published preview over the size limit merges pairs of frames), the gear = Preview motion and the crosshair = Preview position and pivot (both below).
⑪ Save (Ctrl+S) saves it as your script effect (with its preview scene; it shows in the Effects tab of the effects dialog and in the Asset Manager). The Save button is enabled only when there are unsaved changes, and then turns red to stand out; after saving, or with nothing changed, it is dimmed gray. Insert into layer adds it with the preview setting values to the end of the current layer's effects in the main window (all frames, one undo step). If the effects dialog is open or the layer is locked, you only get a message.
⑫ The status button shows the current state by color; click it for details (see Status and check below).
⑬ Check, Upload… and Close. Picking another effect, starting a new script or closing with unsaved edits asks Save, Discard or Cancel (* after the effect name in the window title = edited).
Preview setting values mirror the tool dock's rows and order when inserted: effect-specific settings → easing, repeat and repeat count for animated effects → Later effects: Move pivot along for motion-reporting effects → an uneditable, off Cels after the range: Keep the end look. Labels use the same column layout as the effects dialog. Change easing, repeat, repeat count or pivot motion in preview and choose Set as defaults to write easing, repeat, repeatCount and movePivot to the declaration; restoring app defaults Linear, Once, 1 and true removes those keys. Reset restores source values. Insert on current layer uses the selected preview values.
Preview setting values also have the same On OK [Expand canvas] row as the effects dialog. Turned off, the area outside the chick's canvas (what would be cut off on OK) is dimmed in the preview, as in the effects dialog. Click Set as defaults with it off and the declaration gets expandCanvas: false (turning it on removes the key); the effect is then added with canvas expansion off when newly inserted from the effects dialog or by AI. Use it so effects that rise above the image, such as a campfire, don't grow the canvas on OK (effects already added keep their value).
My effects and published effects
My effects list: two published effects with the author's profile picture and name next to them, an effect made only on this computer, and the grey row of a published effect not on this computer with its download button
⑭ Author of published effects (profile picture and name) · ⑮ Published effect not on this computer
⑭ Effects published with your account (author ID = your handle; when signed out, the last handle you signed in with) show your profile picture (or a person icon) and name together next to the name. Without author details, Published appears there instead, or Published · edited after you changed them. Saving and publishing again makes a new version of the same package.
⑮ Effects published with the current account that aren't on this computer show as grey rows at the bottom of the list. The download button on the right fetches it from the online catalog (checking size and SHA-256), installs and opens it. Clicking the grey row itself doesn't open anything. While signed in, the online catalog is checked when the window opens and when the account changes.
Received effects are read-only
Effects made by others (received script effects) open read-only in the Effect Maker. The source, info, preview chick, frame count, motion, position and pivot, and scene can't be changed, and Save, Upload… and the AI panel are off. You can still try preview setting values, Check and Insert into layer.
Open the effect (turn on Show all if it isn't listed).
Click Copy to My Assets in the bottom row. The received original stays as it is, and your own copy with the same source is created and opened (if you already have your own effect with that source, it opens instead).
Edit and save the copy. The copy is your own asset, so you can publish it too.
The received original keeps getting Store updates. Downloading a higher version from the Store replaces the same effect on this computer without asking, so always make your own copy of an effect you want to change. Effects already placed on project layers keep the source they were inserted with in the project, so updates don't change them (see Asset Manager).
Preview motion
Preview motion window: the motion choice and the per-frame X/Y table
⑯ Motion · ⑰ X/Y per frame
The gear button in ⑩ opens the Preview motion window (its tooltip shows the current motion). Choosing ⑯ None, Right, Left, Up, Down (1 px per frame) or Custom fills ⑰ the table (dimmed); editing the table switches to Custom (−32 to 32 px per frame, right and down are +). OK writes previewMotion into the declaration. The chick is moved only in the preview, the check and the published preview (documents are unaffected), so effects that react to movement, such as afterimages and trails, become visible; ctx.frameSource returns the moved frames too. Without it the chick doesn't move.
End chick (transform effects)
Preview of a transform effect: an end chick is chosen and the frame strip turns the first chick into the other one
⑱ End chick · ⑲ Frame strip
Choosing an ⑱ End chick (info box; first item None) changes previewEndChick in the declaration, and the last frame of the preview, the check and the published preview becomes that chick (both chicks stand feet-aligned on a canvas of the same size). Effects that turn one picture into another over several frames read the end picture with ctx.frameSource(ctx.rangeEnd), so the ⑲ frame strip shows the transformation and Check tests it before you save (see "Effects that use several frames" in Script effects).
Preview position and pivot
Preview position and pivot window: X/Y table for Chick pivot, End chick position (X is 16) and End chick pivot, with a dimmed hint below
The crosshair button in ⑩ opens the Preview position and pivot window (its tooltip shows the current non-zero values, for example "Preview position and pivot: End chick position (16, -6)", or "None" when all are zero). Each of the three rows takes X and Y in px (right and down are +, −64 to 64). Without an end chick the two end rows are dimmed and off (their values are kept but not used). Pivot values are offsets from the default pivot (the chick's center), so moving only the end chick leaves the pivot where it is. OK writes only the changed values into the declaration as previewPivot, previewEndOffset and previewEndPivot ([x, y]; zero removes the key), as one undo step in the editor.
Row What it does
Chick pivot Moves each frame's pivot (ctx.pivot). With an end chick it applies to every frame except the last (the end chick's frame); without one, to all frames.
End chick position Moves the end chick from its place (feet aligned with the first chick).
End chick pivot Moves the pivot of the last frame (the end chick's frame).
These values are used only for previews: the Effect Maker preview, Check, AI previews, the published preview and preview scenes (documents are unaffected). Use them to see and check, before saving, morph and rotation effects that only matter when the two images sit in different places or have different centers. In a preview scene the end chick moves from the scene's chick spot and each frame's pivot is kept inside the scene canvas; without a scene the preview canvas widens to fit the moved chick and pivot.
First, middle and last frames of a morph effect in two groups: on the left the end chick appears where the first chick was; on the right the pixels move 16 px to the right as they change
Left: End chick position (0, 0) · Right: End chick position (16, 0) — first, middle and last of 6 frames in each group
The picture draws the morph example from the ⑲ frame strip (it reads the end picture with ctx.frameSource(ctx.rangeEnd) and moves each pixel). With End chick position 0 it changes in place; moved 16 px to the right, the end picture is read at the moved spot, so the image travels there as it changes.
Preview scene
An effect with a layer setting: code reading it with ctx.layer, the layer picker in Preview setting values and the Preview scene row on the right
⑳ Layer picker · ㉑ Preview scene row
Effects that read other layers (a layer setting read with ctx.layer and so on — landing on a ground, following a path) are previewed on a preview scene. When the source uses the other-layer functions or a scene exists, the ㉑ Preview scene row appears (info box, Edit in main editor, Remove scene, layer names bottom to top with the [Chick] position). Without a scene only the chick is drawn, so the other-layer functions return null.
⑳ The layer picker in Preview setting values lists the scene's layer names top to bottom (without the chick layer). Without a scene it only has (none), with "Add a preview scene to pick one of its layers." dimmed below. Renaming scene layers updates the list.
Edit in main editor: without a scene it creates the default one (canvas of chick width × 3 and height × 2 — 48–256 px, an empty ground layer, 1 frame) and opens it in the main editor as a "Preview scene - effect name" tab. Draw with any tool, add layers and name them. Moving the chick layer changes where the chick stands (by its feet), and another chick is placed with its feet on the same spot. A scene with fewer frames than the preview repeats.
Limits: canvas 256×256, 8 layers, 20 frames (layers × frames must fit a 512×512 grid). Effects, groups and parts in scene layers aren't used. The scene tab doesn't ask to save when closed; what you draw reaches the preview shortly after (the Effect Maker counts it as an edit — save the effect to keep the scene). The scene is saved with the effect, goes into asset files as previews/name.scene.png, and the check, the AI preview and the published preview are drawn on it too. Remove scene asks and removes the scene (closing its tab).
The Effect Maker shrunk to the top-right corner of the main editor while the scene is edited: preview and expand button
㉒ Small preview window
After Edit in main editor, the Effect Maker becomes a ㉒ small preview window in the top-right corner of the main editor so it doesn't cover the canvas, and the focus moves to the main editor. Editing the scene updates the small preview right away. Clicking the preview or the expand button, or closing the scene tab, restores the original size and position; clicking Edit in main editor again while the scene is open shrinks it again.
Status and check
Status button clicked after Check: details with the check result, a warning that it runs on Jint and why, and gradient advice
㉓ Status button · ㉔ Status details
㉓ Status button: green = OK or check passed, yellow = warnings only (runs on Jint, gradient advice, scene couldn't be read), red = errors (with the count), dim = rendering, checking or no script.
㉔ Clicking it shows the details: time per chick frame, the execution path (fast path / Jint, with the line and reason), source and run errors and the check result. Click an error line to jump to that code.
Check: runs the install-time source check and checks the title (1–100 characters), then runs the effect with the declared defaults on all 20 sample chicks × the frame count (with the preview scene, end chick, motion, position and pivot as set) and lists run errors (each one once, "Chick N, step M:") and the slowest frame.
Without run errors it also gives gradient advice for each color setting: it draws with a sample gradient and points out, in a yellow line, color settings that still draw in one color when a gradient is chosen (for color lists the first item, for pair lists the first pair's replacement color; unused color settings are skipped). It is only a recommendation: it doesn't count as a problem and doesn't block publishing — picking colors per pixel with ctx.color makes it go away.
Upload…: saves, and when the check passes opens the Publish online window for this one effect (the short description starts as the declared description and the tags as the declared tags; the preview is made automatically). Effects reading other layers always get the layer-reference tag, and effects reading other frames the frame-reference tag. If the check fails, you are told to open the status button to see the problems.
Rules window
Effect writing rules window: rules, answer format and API list, with the Include the current source checkbox and the Copy button
㉕ Include the current source and Copy
Clicking ④ Rules shows the rules, the answer format and the script API list in a separate window. Turn on ㉕ Include the current source to append the editor's source, and Copy puts it on the clipboard ("Copied the guide." shows briefly). How to use it: copy → paste into another AI such as ChatGPT on the web and describe the effect you want → paste the code block from the answer into the editor as a whole.
The rules cover: one source with one declaration; always writing name, description, tags and language (plus translations.en when not English); determinism (a seed setting for effects that suit randomness); run limits; setting types; adding useful settings without being asked (an anchor — pivot ctx.pivot, center ctx.center or source bounds ctx.source — plus direction, speed, loop, range, offset, color, strength and size, usually 3–8); picking colors per pixel with ctx.color("key", x, y) where possible so gradients are followed (lists ctx.colorAt, pairs ctx.pairColor, bounds { x, y, w, h } when the shape needs it, s.key only when one color is required — with worse/better examples); the fast path; reading other layers only through a layer setting and ctx.layer("key") (not by position or a name in the code, with the preview scene's layer name as the default, handling null); and other frames (transform, ctx.matchPixels, end chick).
Effect Maker rules and AI guidance require a moving effect to report its displacement with ctx.movePivot(dx, dy). Check warns if the resulting image moved without that call in the source, but publishing remains allowed. Scripts containing the call automatically receive the required pivot-move tag on upload; it cannot be removed and counts toward the eight-tag limit.
AI panel
Effect Maker with the AI panel open: conversation, three attach buttons under the input, model list and Send
㉖ Conversation and input · ㉗ Attach buttons · ㉘ Model list and Send
The ⑦ AI button widens the window by the panel's width and opens the AI panel on the right (when maximized, the source area gets narrower). ㉖ Send the effect you want or what to change, and the AI (same Claude Code or Codex login as the AI chat) reads the source → writes the whole source into the editor (one undo step in the editor; drawings and layers stay) → checks it with the preview and Check, following the rules. It adds useful settings on its own and briefly lists them in its answer, makes effects that read other layers with a layer setting, and by default picks colors per pixel so gradients are followed. Saving, inserting into the layer and publishing are up to you with the buttons below. The conversation is gone when you close the window.
The header has the Claude/Codex switch, New chat (the source stays) and Close. If the CLI is missing or needs a login, install or log in with Open AI chat, then click Check again.
㉗ The three buttons under the input attach an image file, the current canvas or the current preview frame; Ctrl+V and drag and drop work too. Click a chip to enlarge or remove it (as in the AI chat).
㉘ The model list left of Send is the same list as the model field in the AI chat header. Changing it shows "Model: … — applies from the next message." and the conversation continues. The chosen AI and model are saved right away and kept the next time; the AI chat shares the same setting (the last choice wins).
Pressing Enter or Send while the AI's turn is running puts the message in the Queued row above the input (first line, image count and a remove button); it is sent in order when the current turn ends (even when stopped). Meanwhile Send shows only an arrow icon. Remove puts the message back into the input when the input is empty, and New chat clears the queue.
The AI panel can look at the open drawing, layers, effects and references but can't change them (the app blocks that with a separate access key for the panel). It reads, writes and checks the Effect Maker source and can read your other script effects for reference ("like my X effect, but …" — it finds and reads it without changing it).
