pages.text:
The Asset Manager handles effect (script effect), effect preset and gradient assets one at a time. It shows the assets you made on this computer and those you received from the Store or files, installs from the Store, exchanges files and publishes your own assets online. Each asset has its own author, license and Store information (Store ID and version). .chickxel-asset package files are only used to move assets: exporting bundles them, and importing or downloading adds the assets inside one by one (a file with several assets adds each separately, inheriting the file's author and license).
Use it to find and install effects and gradients others published in the Store, to get new versions of received assets, to give your effects or presets to a friend as a file, and to share effects you made (see Publish online).
Asset kind Where it is used
Script effect The Effects tab of the effects dialog (see Script effects). Can be published.
Effect preset The Presets tab of the effects dialog (see Effect presets). Exchanged as files only, not published.
Gradient The gradient Presets window and everywhere you pick a gradient (see Gradient). Can be published.
Opening it
Open it with Tools > Asset Manager….
Open Store at the bottom of the Effects tab of the effects dialog opens the Store tab (effects), and the Asset Manager button under the list of the gradient Presets window opens it filtered to gradients. Show in Asset Manager in the right-click menu of an effect box in the effects dialog or of the Effect Maker list opens it with that asset selected.
Click Open in Chickxel on a chickxel.com package page (allow it if the browser asks to open Chickxel) and Chickxel comes to the front (starting if it isn't running), and the Store tab reloads the online list and opens with that package selected. Filters and search are cleared, and nothing is installed until you click Install in the details. If the package isn't in the list (hidden or removed), the status line says the package opened from the website isn't in the online list. Double-clicking a downloaded .chickxel-asset file adds it in the Installed tab just like importing, and selects the asset. If Chickxel is already running, it opens in that window. On Windows, links and double-clicking work after you have started Chickxel once (see Installation).
Installed tab
Installed tab of the Asset Manager: Effects/Gradients filter, search and the Import, Export, Publish and Restore default effects buttons at the top; My assets and Received assets on the left; details and buttons of the selected asset on the right
① Tabs (Installed, Store, Updates) · ② Kind filter (Effects, Gradients) and name search · ③ Import from File, Export, Publish Online, Restore default effects · ④ List · ⑤ Details and buttons of the selected asset
① There are Installed, Store and Updates tabs.
② Filter by Effects / Gradients (Effects at first) and search by name, author or Store name. Effects shows script effects and effect presets together.
③ Import from File… checks a .chickxel-asset file and adds the assets inside one by one. Export… bundles the assets shown in the list into one file (each with its author and Store information; the ones you made get your account as author — a single asset exactly as received from the Store goes out as the same Store package). Publish Online… opens the Publish Online window below. Restore default effects puts back official effects you deleted and raises older versions to the version in the app (edited ones stay; the button is off until it finishes).
④ The list shows My assets (assets made on this computer or whose author ID is your account handle) and then Received assets. Under each name are the author's profile picture (only for assets linked to the Store; a person icon otherwise) and the author's name, followed by the version for received assets, or 'Published 1.0.2' and 'modified' (if changed after publishing) for your published assets. Assets made on this computer show 'Made on this computer' instead of an author name.
⑤ Shows the selected asset's preview (the first frame of the package preview picture if there is one, otherwise the effect animating on a sample picture; gradients as a strip), description, facts (kind, author, license, Store ID, version, modified, source, added, required app version, source hash, script run) and buttons, as listed in the table. Script effects installed through the Asset Manager (import from file or the Store) are trusted on install, so they draw without asking and Script run is Allowed. Only when a script isn't allowed yet — for example one you chose not to run when opening a project — an orange note says the asset contains script effects (never for official effect packages).
Selected asset Buttons
My assets Favorite (gradients), Edit in Effect Maker (script effects), Rename…, Edit parameters (effect presets), Export as Package File…, Publish Online… (Publish New Version… if already published; not for effect presets), Delete. Edited in place.
Received assets Favorite (gradients), Copy to My Assets, Export as Package File…, Open Web Page (when the author has a website), View License (when there is a license file), Delete. Editing makes your own copy; the original keeps receiving updates.
Delete removes the asset right away (there is no restore bin). Official effects that the app installs by default aren't reinstalled once deleted; bring them back with Restore default effects. Effects and gradients already in a project are copied in, so they stay even if you delete the asset.
Importing from a file checks the file list, sizes, checksums, effect settings and preview images first. If anything is wrong, each problem is listed and nothing is added; an asset that needs a newer Chickxel tells you which version. If the same Store asset or an asset with the same content already exists, the Import Asset window asks Replace / Keep Both / Skip, and Apply to the remaining items uses your choice for the remaining overlaps.
On first launch, your old effect presets (formerly custom effects) and gradient presets move into My assets. The old files stay in the settings folder as effect-presets.backup-date.json and gradient-presets.backup-date.json.
Export… and Export as Package File… make package files for exchanging assets. Assets you made get your signed-in account's display name as author.
Store tab
Store tab: Effects/Gradients filter, search, tags, Refresh and Open on Website at the top; online asset list on the left; preview, information and Install button of the selected asset on the right
⑥ Filter, search, tags, Refresh, Open on Website · ⑦ Online list · ⑧ Details of the selected asset and Install
⑥ The online list is downloaded from chickxel.com the first time you open the tab ("Loading the online list…" while loading, then "N assets · time downloaded"). There are the Effects / Gradients filter, search (name, description, author, tags), the All tags list, Refresh and Open on Website (opens the chickxel.com assets page on the tab of the kind you are filtering).
⑦ Each row shows the name and, under it, the author's profile picture and name, the version, the kind and the status (installed version, new version, or can't be installed on this version). Names and descriptions appear in the display language when the package has a translation.
⑧ Preview image, short description, ID, version, installed version, author, license, kind, required app version, size, published, updated, review (Official Chickxel / Reviewed / Community — uploaded by users), tags, and the Install (or Update to …, Show in Installed) and Open Web Page buttons.
Clicking Install shows a progress bar, percentage and Cancel in its place. If the downloaded file doesn't match the checksum in the list, Chickxel only reports an error and changes nothing. An asset that can't be used on this version shows why, for example "Can't install: requires Chickxel 1.20.0 or later", and its Install button is off. If an asset linked to the same Store package is already installed, it is replaced without asking, but only by a higher version (see Store versions and local edits below). Assets from the Store have the source Online catalog.
The 23 official effects such as Outline and Shadow are installed the first time the app starts (source Installed with the app). The Store also has 8 official gradients (Rainbow, Repeating Rainbow, Sunset, Ocean, Transparent Fade, Fire, Forest, Grayscale) and effect presets (Outlined Drop Shadow, Hit Reaction, Shiny Pickup).
Author profile pictures are downloaded only when the Store list has a chickxel.com profile picture address; they are kept small on this computer and reused (official effects use the Chickxel picture). Without a picture, or when it can't be downloaded, a person icon is shown.
Updates tab
Check for updates downloads the online list again and compares it with assets that have Store information (even if imported from a file, when the Store ID matches). Each asset with a new version gets an "Installed 1.0.0 → new version 1.1.0" row and an Update to … button. New versions are installed only when you click, and effects already in projects stay as they are. Local edits are replaced by the new version without asking. The tab name shows the number of updates (e.g. Updates (1)), or "All received assets are up to date." when there are none.
Without an internet connection, the Store and Updates tabs say in orange that the online list couldn't be reached and show the last downloaded list instead. Installed assets keep working.
Store versions and local edits
Assets from the Store stay linked to their Store package and receive updates. Downloading from the Store (Install on the Store tab, the Updates tab, or downloading a published effect in the Effect Maker) works like this:
The package ID and version inside the downloaded file must match the online list, or nothing is installed.
If an asset linked to the same package is already installed, it is overwritten only by a higher version. Local edits are replaced by the new version without asking, and favorites are kept. The same or a lower version isn't installed (nothing is downgraded).
If several assets are linked to the same package (duplicates from earlier), only one is kept.
If it overlaps an unlinked asset with the same content, the Import Asset window asks what to do. Importing from a file asks for every overlap.
To change a received asset, first make your own copy with Copy to My Assets. The copy has no Store link, so updates never overwrite it. Received script effects are read-only in the Effect Maker too (see Effect Maker).
Effects already placed on project layers keep the source and values they were inserted with inside the project, so they don't change when the asset is updated or deleted.
Using received assets
Received effects appear on the Effects tab of the effects dialog, and received effect presets on the Presets tab, together with your own. Their tooltips show the Store name (or the author), and Rename, Parameters and Delete are only for your own (see Effect presets).
In the gradient Presets window, received gradients show the Store name (author) next to their name. Edit one and click Save to My Assets to keep the original and make your own copy (see Gradient).
To modify a received asset, make your own copy with Copy to My Assets in its details.

pages.text:
Turns one of your assets into a public package and uploads it with your Chickxel account (one package per asset). If you aren't signed in, the account window opens first. Publish Online… at the top of the Installed tab opens it for the asset selected in the list (or the only one shown, if none is selected); Publish Online… or Publish New Version… in your asset's details and publishing from the Effect Maker open it for that asset. Received assets can't be published — you're told to copy one to My assets and publish the copy. Effect presets aren't published (chickxel.com doesn't accept them either); publish effects as script effects.
Publish Online window: Author (profile picture, display name and @handle), Package (mode line, name, short description, languages, package ID, version, tag chips) and License CC0-1.0 on the left; the asset to publish, list preview, pre-upload checks and the Upload button on the right
⑨ Author · ⑩ Package · ⑪ License · ⑫ Asset to publish · ⑬ List preview · ⑭ Pre-upload check
⑨ Author: the profile picture, display name and @handle (author ID) of the account you are signed in with are shown together and can't be edited here. Change them in Help > Chickxel Account… (the handle can't change after you upload a package).
⑩ Package: the top line tells whether this is a new package or an update (new package / 'Name update: old → new version' / checking / couldn't check because of the connection — plus a note when a package of yours with the same name gets the new version). Then name, short description (up to 200 characters; scripts are filled in from the declaration's name and description), Languages… (a name and short description per language, shown to people viewing the Store and chickxel.com in that language; languages with text show green with a check), package ID, version and tags. The package ID can't be edited and is set automatically: the ID of your published package if the asset came from it (or a copy of it), otherwise 'handle.name-part' (a short hash if the name has no English letters). The same handle and name means an update, so rename to publish a different package. The version field suggests the next patch version (1.0.0 → 1.0.1). Type tags like #neon and add a chip with Space, Enter or a comma; remove one with its X, or with Backspace in an empty field (up to 8, lowercase English letters, digits and hyphens, 32 characters each; rule breakers turn orange). Effects that read other layers always get the layer-reference tag and effects that read other frames the frame-reference tag pre-filled (can't be removed; counts toward the 8 — if the tags are already full, a check error asks you to remove another tag).
⑪ License: always CC0-1.0. Anyone may copy, change and use the asset without conditions (including commercial use, without credit), and the package includes the CC0 text as LICENSE.txt.
⑫ Asset: the name and kind of the asset being published. It becomes the package's asset.
⑬ List preview: the picture shown in the Store list and details and on chickxel.com. It starts as the asset's preview; replace it with a PNG (up to 512×512, 1 MB) via Replace with Image File… or go back with Use Asset Preview. Effects with a preview scene also upload previews with the scene layers hidden (with and without the effect), which chickxel.com details can switch to with 'Hide helper layers' (the effect still draws as it read those layers; not included when you use your own image). The automatic preview is an animated PNG (APNG) of the effect run over several steps (10 for effect presets, the declaration's previewFrames for script effects, 0.1 s each) on the chosen chick. A step identical to the one before is merged, so an effect that doesn't move becomes a single image. The package also gets the original without the effect, previews/<name>.original.png, so hovering the large picture on the chickxel.com asset page compares the original (left of a vertical line) with the effect (right) — not included when you choose your own picture. Exporting a package adds the same previews; the Asset Manager details and this window show only the first frame.
⑭ Pre-upload check: checked as you type, with the same rules as the server. Red X = error (blocks uploading), orange exclamation mark = warning (you can still upload).
Uploading
With no errors, a blue check says all checks passed and Upload turns on. Click it.
While uploading, a progress bar and Cancel Upload appear. If the server rejects the package, the reason appears at the end of the checks as 'Rejected by the server: …'.
Once uploaded, the package appears right away in the Store list and on the chickxel.com assets page (chickxel.com/packages/<ID>), and a message says it was uploaded. The package page isn't opened automatically: click Open website in the message to open it in your browser (OK just closes). The asset gets Store information, so later uploads become new versions of the same package.
After pressing Upload, its label shows 'Uploading… N%' with the same percentage as the progress bar below. When transfer finishes and the server checks and saves the package, it shows 'Checking on server…' and an indeterminate bar. Upload cannot be pressed again while busy; Cancel upload stops it.
Checks and tags
Main errors: package ID, version (SemVer), name, short description, language settings or tag format; no room for a required tag; no list preview; a name that clashes with another package; a version not higher than the highest one already published (online list and this computer's upload records) — "Enter a version higher than X" (published versions can't change). Warning: no tags.
Uploading a script effect whose source uses ctx.movePivot automatically adds the pivot-move tag. Like layer-reference and frame-reference it cannot be removed and counts toward the eight-tag limit.
Deleting a published package
When a published package is deleted on chickxel.com (by you, by an admin, or through report handling), it disappears from the site, the Store list and your profile, the XP it earned is removed, and its storage quota is returned right away. The server still keeps it, though, so an admin can restore it or delete it permanently. Until an admin does either, the deleted package's ID can't be used again: publishing with the same ID is refused by the server.

Export dialog: settings on the left, output preview on the right, two tabs and the Export button
① Export button · ② Export tab · ③ Import Settings tab · ④ Settings · ⑤ Output preview · ⑥ Divider
The Export dialog sets how the project is exported as PNGs for Unity and other tools. There are two outputs, the frame sheet that lays out the frames and the part atlas that packs part images, and the settings are saved in the project (.chickxel).
Opening and layout
Open it with Ctrl+E or File > Export…. Settings apply as soon as you change them (one undo step per setting), and the blue ① Export button at the bottom closes the dialog and exports. If export on save is on, Ctrl+S alone exports too. There are two tabs: ② Export and ③ Import Settings.
④ Left = settings, ⑤ right = output preview (sheet and cell name list per file). Drag ⑥ the divider to split the width; the dialog size and collapsed sections are remembered.
The window position, size, split ratio and collapsed sections are app settings, so they stay the same in other projects.
Setting sections
Export dialog with all setting sections collapsed
⑦ Common · ⑧ Files · ⑨ Frame sheet · ⑩ Part atlas · ⑪ Advanced
Section Main settings
⑦ Common Output (frame sheet, part atlas, both), skins (current outfit, chosen skins), skin packing, layout (grid, auto layout), sort order, cell count, separate files, cell names, spacing between cells, trim borders, power of two, scale
⑧ Files Export on save, folder, file format (PNG/JPG/TGA/BMP), Unity .meta (off, auto, always)
⑨ Frame sheet Name, Single frame, path
⑩ Part atlas Name, keep original positions, Sprite Library, path
⑪ Advanced Per sheet
The frame sheet and part atlas share the same sheet settings. Turn on ⑪ Advanced > Per sheet to keep separate settings for the part atlas.
Common section
Common section of the Export dialog
⑫ Cell count · ⑬ Order · ⑭ Separate files · ⑮ Cell names · ⑯ Skin and Choose skins
A new project starts with the frame sheet only, grid layout, the current outfit, automatic cell count, 1 px spacing between cells and 1× scale. The numbered settings:
⑫ Cell count (grid layout): auto (smallest sheet), N columns or N rows (1–1024, 4 at first).
⑬ Sort order: drag the part, skin, tag and frame rows or use Alt+↑/↓ to reorder them, and use New row here between rows to set where lines break. Sorting changes only positions; cell names stay the same.
⑭ Separate files: split files per tag and per part (both can be on). Splitting per skin is chosen under Skin packing.
⑮ Cell names: Frame number or By tag (default for new projects). They're used as sprite names in Unity .meta, so changing them shows a warning.
⑯ Choose skins…: choose skins to export, outfit presets and layers to include in the composite.
Setting What it does
Layout Grid places cells of equal size in order; Auto layout packs cells of different sizes tightly.
Max width and packing order (auto layout) The sheet's maximum width (0 = auto) and the order cells are packed in (In sort order or Largest first).
Spacing between cells 0–64 px (1 px at first).
Trim borders Cuts the transparent border off each cell (off at first).
Power of two Rounds the sheet width and height up to powers of two (off at first).
Scale (at the bottom of the Common group, below power of two; 1–16× — type a number or pick 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8): enlarges the frame sheet and part atlas images by a whole number (nearest neighbor, so pixels stay crisp). Cells are cut out first and then enlarged, so cell spacing and maximum width are px in the enlarged result (spacing 1 stays 1px). 9-slice borders and the Unity PPU (Pixels Per Unit in the .meta) are multiplied by the same scale, so the size in Unity stays the same (PPU 16 · scale 3 → 48), and the pivot stays on the same spot. Single frame sheets are enlarged too (canvas × scale). The preview on the right shows the enlarged result; the motion test shows the original size. As a common setting both outputs use it; with per-sheet settings on, the part atlas has its own. It is saved in the project file and export presets; GIF export has its own scale.
Files and per-output settings
Files section: export on save (on at first), folder (empty = the project folder), file format PNG, JPG, TGA or BMP (JPG quality 1–100%, 90 at first), Unity .meta off, auto or always (auto at first = written only inside a Unity Assets folder or where a .meta already exists).
Frame sheet section: name (empty = the project name) and path. Single frame appears only when Sprite Mode in Import Settings is Single; it exports one chosen frame at canvas size (only the scale applies) and ignores the common layout settings.
Part atlas section: name (empty = the frame sheet name + _parts), Keep original positions (auto layout; on at first), Sprite Library (also writes the part .meta) and path.
Turning on Advanced > Per sheet copies the current common values into a second set of settings for the part atlas.
The folder and the sheet and part atlas names are written to the project file encrypted with this install's own key, so this computer's paths aren't revealed. As a result, opened on another computer or by another user, or after the settings folder is deleted, they go back to the defaults (the project folder and the project name) (see File types and where they go).

File > Export as animated GIF… creates a single GIF for sharing. The project and its export settings aren't changed. Save as GIF… in the preview's right-click menu opens the same dialog.
Export as animated GIF dialog: range, zoom, speed, loop, background, preview, result info
① Range · ② Zoom · ③ Speed · ④ Loop · ⑤ Background · ⑥ Preview · ⑦ Output size, frames, duration, colors
Choose tag list opened
⑧ Tag list
Settings
① Range: current tag (disabled when the current frame isn't in a tag), all frames, or ⑧ choose a tag (disabled without tags; the list shows each tag's frames and reverse or ping-pong). It starts with the current tag if there is one, otherwise all frames, and frames follow the tag's direction.
② Zoom: 1–10×, nearest neighbor so pixels stay crisp (initially the zoom that makes the result about 256 px).
③ Speed: Original speed (each frame's own duration, the default), Speed multiplier (0.1–10×, every frame's duration divided by the multiplier — 2× plays twice as fast, 0.5× at half speed) or Fixed FPS (1–50, every frame lasts 1 s ÷ FPS). The ⑥ preview and the ⑦ duration follow the chosen speed; the project's frame durations don't change. Upload to gallery has the same setting.
④ Loop: loop forever or play 1–100 times (1 = once).
⑤ Background: transparent (alpha below 50% becomes transparent, the rest opaque) or composited over a background color.
Speed, loop and background are app settings and stay the same next time (speed is shared with Upload to gallery); range and zoom are worked out again each time the dialog opens.
Preview and saving
⑥ The preview on the right plays at the chosen speed, and ⑦ shows the output size, frame count, duration and color count. GIF frame durations are rounded to hundredths of a second and never shorter than 20 ms (so Fixed FPS goes up to 50). With few enough colors (255 with transparency, otherwise 256) the GIF is lossless; with more, each frame gets its own palette and colors are reduced (no dithering).
Export… opens a save dialog. The default name is <project>.gif next to the project (<project>_<tag>.gif for a tag); a never-saved project uses the last folder you used. After saving, the dialog stays open showing the file size and result, so you can change settings and save again (Cancel becomes Close). You can assign a shortcut in Preferences > Shortcuts.
If compositing the preview frames or writing the GIF takes a while, a dark translucent overlay covers the whole window until it finishes, with Compositing frames or Creating GIF and the percentage with a progress bar in a box in the middle.

⑥ View Gallery at the bottom left opens the chickxel.com gallery in your browser, so you can browse what others have uploaded without uploading anything.
Sharing the editable file
Turn on Also share the editable .chickxel file (off by default) near the bottom of group ① to upload this project's .chickxel file along with the PNG or GIF, so anyone can download it from the picture's page and open and edit it in Chickxel. The shared copy drops this computer's export folder and keeps the sheet and part atlas names as plain names without folders (see File types and where they go). Script effects' source code is included (the window says so when it's on), and people are asked whether to run it when they open the file (see Script effects). The file can be up to 8 MiB; if it's larger, you're told to turn off file sharing and upload only the picture. The gallery post has separate buttons to download the PNG/GIF and the Chickxel file.
Allowing image download
Allow image download (PNG/GIF) (on by default) at the bottom of group ① decides whether visitors to the picture's page on chickxel.com see the PNG/GIF download button. When it's off, only you and admins see that button; the picture itself stays public. Visitors who aren't signed in are sent to the sign-in page when they click that button instead of downloading; after signing in they return to the same picture page and can download by clicking again. It's separate from downloading the editable .chickxel file (Also share the editable .chickxel file above). You can change it later with Edit on the picture's page.
Uploading
Clicking Upload first opens the account window if you aren't signed in. While the picture is being made, Making the picture is shown; while uploading, a progress bar and Cancel Upload appear; when done, the picture's page (chickxel.com/gallery/…) opens in your browser. A file over 4 MB is refused with a hint to lower the scale or upload just the current frame. If you hit the daily upload limit, you're asked to try again in a few minutes. The project isn't changed.
Uploaded pictures earn XP for your account (see Account level). After the upload the app fetches your account again; if your XP went up, the completion message adds the XP gained and your current level, like +10 XP · Lv 3, and "Level up! Lv 3" if you reached a new level (nothing is added if the server doesn't report levels). Once a document is uploaded, the gallery button in the menu bar sparkles again the next time you save it by hand.

① Primary color · ② Secondary color · ③ Right button = eraser · ④ Tool hint in the top bar (Shift+click line and more)
These rules are shared by the brush tools (pencil, gradient pencil, eraser, lighten/darken, dithering, color replace brush) and by the shape, fill and gradient tools. What differs per tool is on that tool's page.
Mouse buttons
The left button paints with the ① primary color and the right button with the ② secondary color. Press X to swap the two colors.
With ③ Right button = eraser on, the right button of the pencil, gradient pencil, shape and fill tools erases instead of using the secondary color. Turn it on in the Options group of the tool options or in Drawing options in the Tools menu. The pencil and gradient pencil follow the eraser's strength and channels; the shape and fill tools always erase completely.
Tools where the buttons mean something else: Dodge/burn lightens with the left button and darkens with the right; with Dithering the right button swaps where the two colors go; the Eyedropper puts the picked color into the primary (left) or secondary (right) color. The Gradient tool drags with the left button only.
Strokes and undo
Everything from pressing a button to releasing it is one stroke, and one stroke is one undo step. The undo history shows the tool name (Lighten or Darken for lighten/darken, the shape name for shapes).
Pressing the other button mid-stroke cancels that stroke and restores the picture to how it was before it. The status bar shows Cancel stroke and nothing is added to the undo history.
Colors painted with the pencil, fill, shape, dithering and color replace brush tools are added to the recent colors in the color panel. Strokes of the eraser, lighten/darken, gradient and gradient pencil, and strokes that paint transparency, are not added.
Using keys
④ The top bar always shows a one-line hint of what the current tool can do. These keys work with the drawing tools:
Key What it does
Shift+click Brush tools: draws a straight line from the end of the last stroke to where you click. While Shift is held, the line is previewed translucently, including brush size and symmetry (Pencil). Shapes: keeps the proportions (15° steps for lines, squares, circles and so on). Gradient: 45° steps.
Alt While held, the tool becomes the eyedropper and clicking picks a color. Releasing it returns to the original tool.
Ctrl While held, the tool becomes the Move tool. Releasing it returns to the original tool.
Ctrl+wheel Changes the brush size by 1. The status bar shows the current size.
[ / ] Decreases or increases the brush size by 1 (1–32).
X Swaps the primary and secondary colors.
Where paint goes
With a selection, painting and erasing happen only inside it.
With symmetry drawing on, every drawing tool except the gradient tool also paints at the mirrored positions (Brush settings).
In tile mode, strokes that cross the canvas edge continue on the opposite side.
If the current layer is locked, nothing is drawn and the status bar shows The current layer is locked and can't be drawn on.
Drawing commands in the Edit menu
The Edit menu opened
⑤ Add outline · ⑥ Replace color · ⑦ Flip/rotate · ⑧ Canvas size
The Edit menu has commands that change the whole picture (or the selection) at once. Each is one undo step.
Command What it does
⑤ Add outline (primary color) (Ctrl+Alt+O) Add outline (with diagonals) Adds a 1-pixel outline: within the selection (or the whole current cel), transparent pixels that touch an opaque pixel above, below, left or right are painted with the primary color. Add outline (with diagonals) also paints pixels that touch diagonally.
⑥ Replace color… (Ctrl+Alt+R) Set Color to replace (the primary color at first) and New color (the secondary color at first) to change every pixel of that color in the current frame of the current layer. All transparent pixels (alpha 0) count as the same color. With a selection, Selection only limits the change to it. To change only where you rub, use the Replace color brush.
⑦ Flip horizontal (selection/cel) (Shift+H) Flip vertical (selection/cel) (Shift+V) Flips the selected pixels, or the current cel when nothing is selected, horizontally or vertically.
⑦ Rotate 90° (selection/canvas) (Ctrl+R) Rotate -90° (selection/canvas) (Ctrl+Shift+R) Rotates the selected pixels by 90° (press Enter to drop them), or the whole canvas with all frames when nothing is selected.
⑧ Canvas size… (Ctrl+Alt+C) Sets the new size and the image position right on the canvas (Canvas size mode).

⑤ Horizontal symmetry (Shift+X) and vertical symmetry (Shift+Y) also draw on the opposite side of the canvas center axis. They apply to every tool that uses symmetry (pencil, gradient pencil, eraser, shapes and so on).

The pencil (B) is the basic drawing tool: it paints pixels in the brush shape along the path you drag. Painted pixels are replaced with the chosen color as-is, never blended. The mouse button decides whether the primary or secondary color is used, and by default the path is joined only sideways and up/down so every pixel touches the next by an edge (pixel steps). Pixel perfect
A curve drawn with pixel perfect off (top) and on (bottom): with it on, the doubled pixels at stair corners are removed
Turn on Pixel perfect (P, the checkbox in the tool options, or Drawing options in the Tools menu) and strokes are joined diagonally; at brush size 1 the doubled L-shaped pixels at stair corners are removed as you draw, leaving a one-pixel line. Pixels painted earlier in the same stroke are never removed, so going back over your path leaves no holes. At brush size 2 or more no pixels are removed. The gradient pencil and the eraser use the same setting.
The same S-curve drawn with pixel perfect off (left, the doubled pixels it removes in red) and on (right)

With it off, every turn of the staircase gets one extra pixel in an L shape, so the line looks thicker in places. With it on, those pixels are removed and the line steps evenly along the diagonals.
Shift+click lines are drawn without doubled pixels to begin with, so pixel perfect does not change them. The corner where the previous stroke meets the line belongs to two different strokes and is not removed.
Pixel steps
Options group in the pencil tool settings: Pixel perfect (off), Pixel steps (Orthogonal), Right button = eraser
① Pixel perfect · ② Pixel steps (Diagonal / Orthogonal)
① Pixel perfect takes priority over pixel steps. When it is on, the Pixel steps row is dimmed and strokes are joined diagonally. The pixel steps choice is kept and used again when you turn pixel perfect off.
② Pixel steps sets how the pixels of a dragged path and of Shift+click lines are joined. Orthogonal (default) joins them only sideways and up/down, so every pixel touches the next by an edge, with an L-shaped corner at each step. Diagonal is the thinnest line, as before, with steps that touch only at corners. The pencil, gradient pencil and eraser share this setting, it is kept for the next launch, and it is separate from the Shape tool's pixel steps.

pages.text:
Drawing rainbow gradient strokes with the gradient pencil while the colors re-spread over the length drawn so far
The Gradient Pencil (Shift+B) draws like the pencil but takes each painted pixel's color from a gradient, spread once from the start of the stroke to its end or repeated at a set interval. It lives in the pencil group slot, so you can also long-press or right-click that slot to pick it.
Shift+click lines, the brush shape and size, pixel perfect, pixel steps, symmetry drawing and the selection work as with the pencil (pixel perfect and pixel steps are the same settings as the pencil's). With Right button = eraser on the right button erases; otherwise it paints the gradient like the left button.
Colors painted with the gradient pencil are not added to the recent colors.
Gradient settings
Gradient pencil tool options: mode (Repeat), interval, Presets and Default buttons, stop editor
① Mode · ② Interval (Repeat only) · ③ Presets · Default · ④ Stop editor
① Mode: Whole stroke (default) spreads the gradient once from the start of the stroke to its end; Repeat starts again from the first color every interval.
② Interval (2–512px, default 16): the stroke length of one pass through the gradient in Repeat mode. It appears only when Repeat is selected.
③ Presets: pick one of your gradient presets or a gradient from an enabled package, or save the current gradient. Default resets to a black → white gradient.
④ The stop bar, position, color, interpolation, color space and dithering are edited with the same editor as the gradient tool (the down-arrow button at the right end of the bar, or right-clicking the bar, also opens the preset menu). The settings are kept separately from the gradient tool and survive restarts.
How colors are assigned
The default mode, Whole stroke, re-spreads the gradient over the length drawn so far while you draw and fixes start → end colors when you release. Choose Repeat to repeat the gradient at a set interval.
Length is measured along the path the mouse took, not as the straight distance between start and end. Opacity stops replace pixels with that value as the pencil does, without blending, so a fully transparent part erases what is below.

Built-in sets added in a newer version appear automatically in an older sets file, while built-in sets you deleted stay deleted until you restore them.

pages.text:
A picture made with the shape pen: leaves along a pencil branch, grass and flowers along the ground and sparkles in the sky
Made with built-in sets: leaves (dragged along the branch, optimized spacing) · grass (dragged along the ground) · flowers and sparkles (clicks)
The Shape Pen stamps small pictures (shapes) from the chosen set. Use it when you need many slightly different copies of the same kind of thing, such as leaves, grass, flowers, sparkles or pebbles. It is the third tool in the pencil group slot: pick it from the list you get by long-pressing or right-clicking the slot, or from the Tools menu (no default shortcut).
Click to stamp the next shape centered where you pressed. Shapes keep their own colors and opacity: transparent pixels leave what is below untouched and semi-transparent pixels blend with it. Even-sized shapes extend one pixel further right and down from the center, like the brush.
Drag to keep stamping at each spacing (or with optimized spacing). One stroke is one undo step. The shape that will be stamped next is shown semi-transparent with an outline under the cursor.
Symmetry drawing (mirrored positions get a flipped shape), tile mode, the selection, locked layers, linked cels and drawing outside the canvas work as with the pencil. Alt+click picks a color.
Shape pen settings
Shape pen tool options: set picker and set buttons, shape tiles, Add shape and delete, Order, Spacing, Optimized spacing, Tint with current color
① Set · ② Set buttons · ③ Shape tiles · ④ Add shape and delete shape · ⑤ Order · ⑥ Spacing · ⑦ Optimized spacing · ⑧ Tint with current color
In the Shape pen group of Tool options you choose the set to stamp and how it is stamped.
Item What it does
① Set Chooses the set to stamp. Each row of the list shows the set's first shape and its name.
② Set buttons From the left: new set, rename, delete set (red button, asks first — cannot be undone), restore built-in sets, Export set… and Import sets….
③ Shape tiles The set's shape tiles. The highlighted tile is the shape stamped next, and the highlight moves on with each stamp. Click a tile to stamp that shape next. Right-click a tile, or press the red trash button, to delete the shape (built-in sets' shapes can be deleted too).
④ Add shape Adds shapes from the selection, the current cel or PNG files (see “Adding shapes” below).
⑤ Order How the next shape is chosen (table below). Remembered per set; dimmed when the set has only one shape.
⑥ Spacing The distance between stamps while dragging (px, 1 or more, default 1). At 1 every pixel passed over gets a stamp, giving an overlapping continuous trail. Dimmed while optimized spacing is on.
⑦ Optimized spacing When on (the default), each next shape is stamped at the first position where it no longer overlaps the previous stamp, so stamps follow the drag direction touching but not overlapping.
⑧ Tint with current color When on, keeps the shape's shading and opacity but changes its color to the primary color (the secondary color with the right button). Off by default.
Built-in sets
The shapes of the twenty built-in shape pen sets, one set per strip
From the top left, two sets per row: Leaves · Autumn leaves · Pine needles · Grass · Flowers · Petals · Sparkles · Stars · Dots · Bubbles · Clouds · Pebbles · Bricks · Raindrops · Snowflakes · Hearts · Puffs · Wood grain · Cracks · Coins and gems
Twenty built-in sets come with the app, each with 6–10 shapes. Autumn leaves mix orange, red and yellow, flowers pink, blue and white, stars gold and white, and hearts red and pink; sparkles, bubbles, puffs, raindrops, wood grain, cracks and petals contain semi-transparent pixels. Only the dots set uses the In order order; the others are Random.
Built-in sets can also have shapes deleted, be renamed or be deleted entirely. The restore built-in sets button asks first, then puts deleted built-in sets back and resets the built-in sets to their original shapes, names and order (your own sets stay as they are). Built-in sets added in a newer version appear automatically in an older sets file, while built-in sets you deleted stay deleted until you restore them.
Adding shapes
The menu of the Add shape button adds shapes to the chosen set (if there is no set at all, a new one is created). The shape you added becomes the next shape to stamp.
From selection: adds the selected pixels of the current cel as a shape (only when there is a selection).
From current cel: adds the whole current cel as a shape.
From PNG files…: pick one or more PNG files and add them all at once.
Either way the transparent border is trimmed and opacity is kept. Images with only transparent pixels, or with a side longer than 256px, are not added and the status bar says why. Create a new set (the + button) to collect shapes you drew yourself.
Order
Order is remembered separately for each set.
Order What it does
Random Picks any shape from the set for each stamp. The same shape never comes twice in a row.
In order Stamps the set's shapes in order, going back to the first after the last.
Selected Always stamps only the chosen (highlighted) shape tile.
Spacing and optimized spacing
The same wavy path stamped with the leaves set at spacing 1 (left) and with optimized spacing (right)
Left: spacing 1 (optimized spacing off) · Right: optimized spacing
Spacing 1 stamps at every pixel passed over, so the shapes overlap densely into a continuous trail like a bush or fur. Optimized spacing measures overlap with the shape's opaque pixels (the transparent border does not count, and a different next shape is measured as itself) and stamps at the first position with no overlap, so each shape stays visible and touches the next even when sizes differ. To set the distance yourself, turn optimized spacing off and raise the spacing (px).
Tinting and the right button
With Tint with current color on, the most common color in the shape becomes the primary color and the other colors keep their saturation and brightness ratios to it, so the shading (outlines and highlights) stays. Use it to stamp autumn leaves or a different green from the green leaves set. The right button tints with the secondary color. When off, both buttons stamp the shape's own colors.
With Right button = eraser on, the right button erases in the shape, by each shape pixel's opacity.
Exporting and importing sets
Export set…: saves the chosen set as a single .chickxel-shapes file. The set's name is suggested as the file name, and built-in sets can be exported too.
Import sets…: pick one or more files; each becomes a new set added to the end of the list, and the last one is selected. Existing sets are never overwritten, and a name already in use gets (2), (3)… appended. A plain PNG can be picked too: it becomes a set holding that one image as a shape (transparent border trimmed, named after the file). The status bar shows each imported set's name and shape count, and files that could not be read are listed together in one message.
Dropping a .chickxel-shapes file onto the main window (where the canvas does not take it) also switches to the shape pen and imports the set.
A set file holds the set's name, order and shapes (PNG, transparency kept), so you can share it with others or move it to another computer.
Where sets are stored
Sets are saved on every change in a single file, <settings folder>/Chickxel/ShapePen/shape-sets.json (each set's name, order and shapes); the chosen set, spacing, optimized spacing and tinting are kept in the settings. If the file is damaged, it is moved to shape-sets.json.bad and the built-in sets are used.

One pass at 50% halves the alpha, and releasing and rubbing again halves what is left (the checkerboard shows through). With only R on nothing becomes transparent; only the red component is removed, so the red band turns almost black, the white band turns cyan, and the green and blue bands change only slightly.

runs.t: An example with only R on. The red area loses its R and turns black, the green area has no R and stays the same, and the blue area loses only the bit of red mixed into it, so its color shifts slightly. No pixel becomes transparent.

pages.text:
Rubbing out a gray gradient with the eraser, then holding Shift and clicking to erase in straight lines
The Eraser (E) erases the pixels along your drag to transparent, in the brush shape. Both the left and right buttons erase. A lower strength fades pixels gradually, and choosing channels removes only certain colors.
While you hold Shift, the line from the end of the last stroke to the mouse pointer is previewed translucently; click to erase along it (same as straight lines with the pencil).
The eraser remembers its own brush shape and size, separate from the pencil (Brush settings). Pixel perfect and Pixel steps in the tool options are the same settings as the pencil's, so by default it erases along a path joined sideways and up/down, and with pixel perfect on it joins diagonally (removing doubled pixels at size 1). The selection and symmetry drawing work as with the pencil.
Erase strength and channels
Erase group in the eraser tool settings: Strength 100%, channels R, G and B all on

Channels R, G, B: with all on it erases to transparent; with some on, alpha stays and only the chosen color channels are reduced by the strength. With none on, nothing is erased.

Drawing with the right button in the pencil or gradient pencil with Right button = eraser on follows these strength and channel settings. Right-button erasing with the shape and fill tools always erases completely, whatever the settings.

pages.text:
Tool options of the Shape tool: shape buttons with the star selected, drawing hint, points and Fill
① Shape buttons · ② Drawing hint · ③ Per-shape count (star Points) · ④ Fill
The Shape tool (R) draws 11 shapes by dragging, from lines and curves to stars and cubes. The shape spans from where you press to where you release, and the result is previewed while you drag. The left button draws with the primary color and the right button with the secondary color (or erases with Right button = eraser on); line width, pen shape and symmetry work as in Brush settings.
Shape settings
① Pick the shape to draw with the shape buttons. L switches straight to the Shape tool's line.
② The line under the shape buttons explains how to draw the chosen shape and what Shift does.
③ Set Corners (3–32) for the Regular polygon, Points (3–32) for the Star and Turns (1–10) for the Spiral.
④ Turn on Fill (U) to paint the inside too; the shape button icons turn filled as well. Lines, curves and spirals can't be filled.
How to draw each shape
Shape How to draw
Line From where you press to where you release. Shift = 15° steps
Curve Drag to set both ends, release, then move the mouse to bend it (the middle of the curve passes through the mouse; it's only a preview until confirmed). Click the same button or press Enter to confirm; the other button, Esc or Ctrl+Z cancels. Shift = 15° steps while dragging the ends, and a circular arc through both ends and the mouse while bending
Rectangle The dragged box. Shift = square
Ellipse An ellipse that fits the dragged box. Shift = circle
Equilateral triangle The dragged line becomes one side (drag right to point up, left to point down). Shift = 30° steps
Isosceles triangle Fits the dragged box. Drag down for the tip on top, up for the tip at the bottom. Shift = equilateral proportions
Regular polygon With the set number of corners (5 = pentagon, 6 = hexagon), fitted to the dragged box. Shift = keep it regular
Star With the set number of points, fitted to the dragged box. Shift = keep it regular
Spiral A spiral that winds outward from the center to fill the dragged box; drag left to wind the other way. Never filled. Shift = square
Cylinder Top ellipse, both sides and the front half of the bottom. Shift = square
Cube A cube with three faces in 2:1 isometric lines. Shift = square
Pixel steps (lines and curves)
Shape tool options with the line selected: Pixel steps Diagonal and Orthogonal
⑤ Pixel steps: Diagonal / Orthogonal
⑤ Lines and curves have Pixel steps: Diagonal (default) also joins pixels diagonally for the thinnest line, while Orthogonal steps only sideways or up/down so every pixel touches the next by an edge.
The same two lines and one curve drawn with Pixel steps Diagonal (left) and Orthogonal (right)
Left: Diagonal · Right: Orthogonal
Diagonal joins pixels that touch only at a corner, giving the thinnest line; Orthogonal adds a pixel at every turn so each pixel touches the next by an edge. A fill with Connect diagonally too (8 directions) on leaks through the corner gaps of a diagonal line, so draw outlines you will fill that way with Orthogonal.

① Text box (dashed border with eight handles) · ② Font · ③ Add font · Open font folder · ④ Size · bold · italic · ⑤ Alignment · ⑥ Letter and line spacing · ⑦ Width and height scale · Smooth
The Text tool (T, the T slot on the toolbar) types text right on the canvas. When you finish, a new layer named after the first line is created just above the current layer (or its group for a part), with one Text effect. One edit is one undo step, and empty text creates no layer.
Creating a text box and typing
Drag = ① text box: lines wrap by word within the box width, and the letter size becomes the size at which one line fits the box height (the Size field in the tool settings changes to match). Click = a single line whose width fits automatically (size from the tool settings). Clicking existing text puts the cursor there to edit it (a locked layer only shows a notice).
Letters appear as pixels as you type, including Korean syllables being composed at the cursor. Use the arrow keys and Home/End (Shift = select, Ctrl/⌥ = by word), Ctrl/⌘+A, C, X, V, double-click = word and triple-click = everything. Enter = new line; Esc, Ctrl/⌘+Enter or clicking outside = finish.
The eight handles on the dashed border resize the box (auto-width text becomes a text box). Dragging the top or bottom edge (corners included) also changes the letter size so all the text fits the new height; the left and right edges change only the width. Drag the border to move it.
Text
Changes in the Text group of the tool settings apply to the text being edited right away.
② Font: the pixel fonts built into the app and fonts you added.
③ Add Font… copies a .ttf, .otf, .ttc or .bdf file into the Fonts folder in the app settings folder and adds it to the list. Open Font Folder opens that folder.
④ Size (0 = the font's own size): pixel fonts work at any size too (scaled cell by cell so the line height becomes that size; strokes may drop out below the original size). The buttons next to it are bold and italic.
⑤ Alignment: left, center, right.
⑥ Letter spacing and line spacing (px).
⑦ Width and height scale 25–400%, and Smooth (vector fonts only — semi-transparent edges).
Fonts
The font list in the Text tool settings opened: Galmuri, NeoDunggeunmo, Unifont, Cozette, Spleen
⑧ Font list (built-in fonts first)
⑧ The font list starts with the built-in fonts: Galmuri 7, 9, 11, 11 Bold, 11 Condensed and 14; Galmuri Mono 7, 9 and 11; NeoDunggeunmo, NeoDunggeunmo Code and NeoDunggeunmo Pro (pixel-style vector fonts — 16px at size 0, sharpest at multiples of 16); Unifont (16px, almost every Unicode character); Cozette (13px Latin and symbols); Spleen 5×8, 6×12 and 8×16 (Latin). All are under free licenses (SIL OFL 1.1, MIT, BSD), so you can use them freely in your art and games; the license texts are in the app folder's Licenses/.
Only the font name is saved in the project. If that font isn't on this computer, a warning appears under the font field and Galmuri11 is used. Characters missing from a font are also drawn with Galmuri11 (for example Korean in Cozette or Spleen).
Text layers
Text is added as a layer effect, not as pixels. Font, size, position, box size and settings such as typing in letter by letter can also be changed in the Text effect in the Effects window, and dragging with the Move tool (no selection, current cel empty on a text layer) moves the text. To turn it into pixels, use Merge down or Bake in the Effects window.

pages.text:
The Eyedropper (I) picks a color from the canvas and sets it as the primary or secondary color right away. Use it to reuse a color already in the picture without opening the palette or the color picker.
Picking colors
Left-click picks into the primary color and right-click into the secondary color. Hold the button and drag to keep picking the color under the pointer; the color where you release stays.
Source: All visible layers (default) picks the composite color you see, and Current layer picks only the current layer's pixel. While a selection is floating, its pixels are picked first. This works like the fill tool's source (Fill).
Clicking outside the canvas picks the color of a normal layer's pixels outside the canvas, and picks nothing where there are none.
Temporary eyedropper with Alt
While using a drawing tool, hold Alt and the pointer over the canvas turns into an eyedropper; click to pick a color without switching tools. Left-click sets the primary color and right-click the secondary color, using the eyedropper tool's Source setting. Releasing Alt returns to the original tool. An Alt used this way, or during a drag, doesn't open the menu bar when released, so the next Enter goes to the canvas (applying a transform and so on), not to the menu.
Tools that support Alt+click: Pencil, Gradient Pencil, Eraser, Fill, Gradient, Shape, Dodge/burn, Dithering and the Replace color brush.
In the text, selection, move, pivot and 9-slice tools, holding Alt does not switch to the eyedropper.

Dithering tool options with the Pattern list open: Checker (50%), Sparse (25%), Dense (75%)
① Pattern list
The Dithering tool paints the pixels under the brush alternately with the primary and secondary colors following a pattern. Use it to hand-paint dithering, the pixel-art technique of mixing two colors in a checker-like dot pattern so they read as an in-between color from a distance. Pick it from its toolbar slot; it has no default shortcut.
The left button paints the primary color on the pattern pixels and the secondary color on the rest. The right button swaps where the two colors go.
The pattern is a 2×2 ordered dither fixed to canvas coordinates, so overlapping or separate strokes always line up into one continuous pattern.
The brush shape and size, symmetry drawing, the selection and Shift+click lines work as with the pencil. Both colors are painted as-is without blending, and the undo history shows Dithering.
Patterns
① Pattern: the share of the primary color. Checker (50%) (default) uses every other pixel, Sparse (25%) one pixel in four and Dense (75%) three pixels in four. The pattern is kept for the next launch.
12×12 pixels painted in navy (primary) and sky blue (secondary) with the Checker, Sparse and Dense patterns
From left: Checker (50%) · Sparse (25%) · Dense (75%); primary = navy, secondary = sky blue
Painting the three patterns side by side gives a hand-made four-step transition from the secondary to the primary color. For a dithered gradient painted in one drag, use the dithering setting of the gradient tool.
Where Chickxel uses dithering
Dithering shows an in-between color through the ratio of dots instead of mixing colors, so it does not add colors to the palette. Besides this tool, the following features offer the same method (Bayer ordered dithering):
Feature Dithering setting
Dithering Paints three 2×2 patterns with the brush
Gradient · Gradient Pencil Dithering: None / 2×2 Bayer / 4×4 Bayer — mixes only the two neighboring stop colors in a pattern
Convert to palette colors No dithering / Ordered dithering (Bayer 4×4) — mixes in a pattern while converting the picture to palette colors
Pixelate AI image Dither in the palette step: None / Bayer 2×2 / Bayer 4×4

The Replace color brush (C) repaints, where you rub, only the pixels of the same color as the pixel where the stroke started. Other colors such as outlines or highlights stay even when the brush passes over them, so use it to recolor a single color or paint only over that color.
How it decides
The color to replace is the color of the pixel where you pressed the button. It does not change even if the stroke passes over other colors.
Only exactly the same color is replaced; there is no tolerance. To include similar colors, use the tolerance of the fill tool or the magic wand.
The left button replaces with the primary color and the right button with the secondary color.
Starting on a transparent pixel paints only transparent pixels, so you can fill empty space behind the drawing without touching it.
What it shares with other brush tools
The brush shape and size, symmetry drawing, the selection, Shift+click lines and the Alt+click eyedropper work as with the pencil. One stroke is one undo step, shown in the history as Color replace brush.
Compared with Replace color in the Edit menu
Replace color… in the Edit menu (Ctrl+Alt+R) changes one color across the whole current cel (or the selection) at once. This brush changes only where you rub, so use it to change just part of a color (see the Edit menu commands in Drawing basics).

pages.text:
The Move tool (V) moves the selected pixels when there is a selection, and the whole current cel otherwise. On normal layers, pixels pushed past the canvas edge are not deleted; they are kept as pixels outside the canvas and come back when you move them in again.
Moving
Action Result
Drag on the canvas With a selection, dragging anywhere moves the selected pixels; without one, it moves the whole current cel, and on a normal layer the layer pivot moves along with the drawing. On a text layer it moves the text (Text). Locked layers are not moved.
Right-drag without a selection Moves only the drawing and leaves the layer pivot where it is. The temporary Move tool you get by holding Ctrl in another tool works the same way.
Arrow keys / Shift+arrow keys Moves by 1px / 8px. When shifting the whole cel, each key press is one undo step.
Hold Ctrl (⌘ on macOS) and drag while using another tool The Move tool is active only while the key is held; releasing it returns to the previous tool. This doesn't happen in the group view, in transform or canvas size mode, or while typing text.
Select several cels in the timeline, then drag or use the arrow keys Without a selection, every selected cel moves by the same amount (one undo step), and the status bar shows how many other cels moved. Groups, empty cels and locked layers are skipped. Transform mode (Ctrl+T) changes only the current cel, so use the Move tool to shift several cels together.
Cycle
The sample image shifted 20 pixels to the right, compared side by side with wrap off and wrap on
Left: wrap off (the part pushed out is kept outside the canvas, shown faded) · Right: wrap on (it comes back on the other side). The light-blue line is the canvas border.
Cycle in the Move tool settings (menu Tools → Drawing options → Move: wrap around) is off by default. Turn it on to have pixels that leave one side of the cel come back on the other side, which helps when lining up seamless patterns (tiles).
With wrap on, pixels outside the canvas are not used, and a part wraps within its own part area. Moving a selection never wraps.
Pixels outside the canvas
Cels of normal layers keep the pixels that leave the canvas. The parts outside are kept when you drag or push layer contents off the canvas with the Move tool, drop a selection outside the canvas, paste and drop an image larger than the canvas, or place an image (dropping it on the canvas, or Apply in the pixelate window) that is larger than the canvas or sticks out of it. Whether you apply the transform mode that follows placing with Enter or keep the image as placed with Esc, the part outside stays as pixels outside the canvas. Up to 4096px around the canvas is kept; pixels farther out are discarded. Parts use only their own part area.
With the Move tool selected, the current layer's pixels outside the canvas are shown faded (40%) around the canvas. While dragging layer contents the whole moved cel is shown, and for a floating selection the part outside the canvas is shown faded. Compositing, the preview, exports and effects use only what is inside the canvas.
Duplicating a layer or frame copies pixels outside the canvas too, and merging down also merges the upper layer's pixels outside the canvas. Shrinking the canvas size keeps the cut parts as pixels outside the canvas, so they come back when you enlarge it again, and the outside part of a placed image also appears when you enlarge the canvas. These pixels are saved in the project file and the undo history (older versions of Chickxel don't read them).
Drawing outside the canvas
A red pencil stroke drawn from inside the canvas out past its right edge and back, shown clearly outside the canvas as well
A pencil stroke drawn past the canvas edge (outside the gray checkerboard is outside the canvas)
With a normal layer selected, while you use a drawing tool (Pencil, Gradient Pencil, Shape Pen, Eraser, Shape, Dodge/burn, Dithering, Replace color brush, Fill) or the Eyedropper, that cel's pixels outside the canvas are shown clearly at the layer's opacity (semi-transparent for a hidden layer), and you can paint, erase and pick colors on them directly. The brush cursor, symmetry ghost cursors, the Shift line preview and strokes all continue outside the canvas. Other layers' pixels outside the canvas are not shown, and export and the preview still use only the inside of the canvas.
Pixels painted outside the canvas are recorded in one undo step together with the part inside. Painting creates or enlarges the pixels outside the canvas, and erasing all of them removes them. Linked cels change too.
You can draw up to 4096 pixels around the canvas. Fill only fills the side you click (clicking outside the canvas fills within the rectangle around the pixels outside the canvas, with canvas pixels as walls), and the eyedropper (including Alt+click) picks colors from pixels outside the canvas. With a selection or in tile mode only the canvas (inside the selection) is painted, and the gradient tool always paints only inside the canvas. A part is drawn only within its own part area.

With it on, changing the pivot with the numbers, buttons or a canvas drag shifts this frame and every later frame by the same amount. Differences that already existed between frames are kept, and earlier frames don't change.
Turning it off removes the separate pivots and positions from the current frame to the end, so those frames follow the target's default pivot again (the part pivot and base position for a part).
Separate pivots are also created in these cases (the box then shows as on in that frame): applying transform mode without a selection (that frame's pivot follows the drawing — or, when a part is only moved, that frame's part position moves), and permanently applying an effect such as shake or float with Move pivot along on to a part (the part position moves per frame by the motion, while the image stays in place in the cel).
Target
⑤ The top of the pivot group in Tool options names the pivot you are changing. The Pivot tool edits the pivot of the current layer selected in the timeline; clicking the Canvas W×H text in the chip at the top left of the timeline edits the canvas pivot instead (the text gets a highlight border). Clicking a layer name or selecting another layer goes back to the layer pivot.

Part That part's pivot (its part atlas sprite), measured against the part size. Target: part "name" (width×height, part atlas)
Group That group's pivot, measured against the canvas. In the group view each part's pivot is shown in blue and dragging on the canvas moves parts instead of the pivot (Arranging), so set the group pivot with the ② buttons and ③ numbers. Select a part to change its pivot. Target: pivot of group "name" (canvas space, width×height)
Canvas pivot (the Canvas W×H text in the chip) The canvas's own pivot used for sheet and Unity exports, measured against the canvas. With a representative layer, the canvas pivot in each frame is that layer's pivot in that frame. Target: canvas pivot (export, all frames)
While the canvas pivot is the target, a Representative choice (None (canvas's own pivot) plus the layers) appears below the target text. Pick a layer and the canvas pivot in each frame follows that layer's pivot in that frame (target text Target: canvas pivot = pivot of representative layer "name"); edits then change that layer's pivot. The representative layer gets a small crown before its name in the timeline, and you can also set it with Use as canvas pivot representative / Stop using as canvas pivot representative in the layer's right-click menu (one undo step).
⑥ Cels with their own pivot show an orange diamond at their top left in the timeline: always for parts (cels with their own part pivot or position), and only in the current layer's row for normal layers and groups. The diamond on frame headers appears only while the canvas pivot is the target, on frames with their own canvas pivot. The part position menu and the status bar show the position in the current frame; changing that position moves all frames by the same amount.
Frame header menu
Right-clicking a timeline frame header handles just that frame: Use a separate pivot for this frame only keeps the current pivot as that frame's own pivot, and Reset pivot to default removes that frame's own pivot. Both apply to the current pivot target (the current layer or the canvas pivot).
Pivot moved by effects
While effects are shown on the canvas, if an effect such as shake moves the image, the pivot mark is drawn where the effect moved it (the center later effects actually use). With the Pivot tool, the original spot that the tool edits is also shown with a small circle and a dotted line.
Where pivots are used: the canvas pivot (or the representative layer's pivot, if set) is the sprite Pivot for Unity exports and sheets; a layer's pivot is the starting rotation center of transform mode and Transform whole layer, Around pivot in symmetry drawing, and the center for that layer's layer effects (rotate, move pivot, script ctx.pivot and so on use that layer's pivot in that frame). Canvas size mode and flipping or rotating the canvas move every layer pivot and the canvas pivot with the image; Transform whole layer moves all of that layer's pivots, transform mode without a selection moves that frame's pivot, and a left drag with the Move tool moves the layer pivot of the moved frames (right-drag to move only the drawing and leave the pivot in place).
Older .chickxel files from before layer pivots are converted on opening without asking. Each normal layer and group gets a copy of the old canvas pivot (default and per frame), so nothing looks different; the canvas pivot stays the same and there is no representative layer. Saving writes the new format, which older versions of Chickxel can't open.

pages.text:
This chapter covers the whole path of a file: opening it, keeping your work safe while you edit, saving, and exporting outputs. Everything you edit lives in a single project file (.chickxel); outputs for game engines or other programs, such as PNG and .meta files, are rebuilt from it every time you save.
Open: a .chickxel opens as is; PNGs, other images, animations and videos are imported as new projects (Opening files). Images dropped on the canvas become layers (Dropping images onto the canvas).
While you edit: files that were saved before are saved automatically when you pause (Autosave), and undo history survives closing the file (Undo history that survives closing). To throw all edits away, use Revert to saved.
Save: Ctrl+S writes the .chickxel and, depending on the export settings, the images and .meta files too (Saving). Cell names are covered in Export cell names, and old outputs that are no longer produced in Cleaning up old outputs. For the export settings themselves see Export dialog; for GIFs see Export as animated GIF.
Close: closing unsaved documents or quitting gathers them in one dialog that asks whether to save (Save prompt when closing).
Preferences and the settings folder are in Preferences; unexpected errors, logs and recovery files are in When errors occur.
Chickxel works with two kinds of files: the project file, which is the editable source, and the outputs made from it when you save or export. Outputs are rebuilt on every save, so always edit the project file. Opening an exported PNG opens the project that made it (Opening (importing) PNGs).
File Role
.chickxel The project file (editable source). Layers, effects, frames, tags, parts, skins, outfit presets and export settings are all stored only here. Double-clicking it in Explorer or Finder opens it in Chickxel.
Exported images (PNG, etc.) The output: frame sheets and part atlases written as PNG (default), JPG, TGA or BMP, for use in Unity or other programs.
.meta The meta file Unity reads (sprite cells, pivot, 9-slice border, etc.). It is named after the image with .meta appended (hero.png.meta).
.spriteLib Unity Sprite Library. Created only when turned on (see Parts · skins).
.gif An animation made separately with File > Export as animated GIF…. Saving doesn't create it (Export as animated GIF).
.chickxel-asset Asset package file. Bundles script effect, effect preset and gradient assets for moving them; importing it in the Asset Manager or double-clicking it in Explorer or Finder adds the assets inside one by one.
Where outputs go
Unless you change the folder or name in the export dialog, outputs are created next to the project and named after it. Saving hero.chickxel gives:
Output Default name Created when
Frame sheet hero.png Export on save is on (the default for new projects)
Part atlas hero_parts.png The project has parts and part atlas export is on (Export: frame sheet and part atlas)
Meta files hero.png.meta, hero_parts.png.meta Depending on Write .meta and the folder (Saving)
Sprite Library One per group and skin Sprite Library is on (Unity Sprite Library)
Exporting separate files per tag, skin or part creates several files named after the project followed by that name. The folder can be a path relative to the project folder or a full path; empty means the project folder (Export dialog).
What's inside a project file
A .chickxel is a ZIP archive. It holds project.json with the structure and settings, plus a PNG for every cel that has pixels (layer × frame, and per skin if there are skins); empty cels aren't stored. Pixels pushed outside the canvas are saved too. Every save also adds the composited first frame (at most 256 px on the long side) as thumbnail.png. Chickxel doesn't use it when opening the file; only the Windows Explorer preview reads it (see Explorer previews in Opening files).
The export folder and export names (sheet name and part atlas name) are written with export path encryption, locked with a key that belongs to this install. The file only shows chickxel-enc:v1:…, so giving a .chickxel to someone doesn't reveal your folder names or user name. The key is made at random the first time you save and kept in local-path-key.bin in the settings folder (on Windows encrypted so only your user can unlock it; on macOS and Linux readable only by your user).
The same user on the same computer gets them back as is. Opened on another computer or by another user, they can't be unlocked and the defaults are used (the project file's folder and the project name). Deleting the settings folder (including when you delete it while reinstalling) also resets the export folder and names of projects saved earlier to the defaults. Older files with plain paths are still read and are encrypted the next time you save.
Projects saved by this version use a new .chickxel format (format version 5) that stores a pivot for every layer, so older versions of Chickxel can't open them. Effects are stored by stable type IDs, so effects this version doesn't know (for example, ones added in a newer Chickxel) aren't drawn but are kept when you save, and script effect sources are saved inside the project file (see Script effects).
Files in the older format without layer pivots, and effect presets, still open. Older-format files are converted without asking: every normal layer and group gets a copy of the old canvas pivot (the default pivot and any per-frame pivots), so nothing looks different; the canvas pivot stays as it was and there is no representative layer (see Pivot tool). The status bar message for opening ends with Converted from the older format (version N), and when the app reopens your last tabs at startup it reports how many files were converted. Saving writes the new format, which older versions of Chickxel can't open.
A file in a format version from a newer Chickxel isn't opened; you're told This file was made with a newer Chickxel (format version N). Update the app in that case (Updates). .gpixel files from the app's former name (Gpixel) open as projects too.
Undo history, the app trash and preferences are kept separately in the app settings folder, not in the project file (Preferences).

pages.text:
Each file opens in its own document tab. Opening a file that is already open switches to its tab instead of creating a new one, and the status bar shows Already open. Whichever way you open a file, it is handled the same way for its file type.
Ways to open
Method How
File menu File > Open (.chickxel · image · GIF · video)… (Ctrl+O). Pick several files at once to open a tab for each.
Recent files Pick from File > Recent files or double-click a recent file on the start screen. Up to 10 recently opened or saved files are remembered; Clear list at the end of the list empties it. Picking a file that no longer exists tells you and removes it from the list. Folders are remembered separately (10) in Recent folders.
File browser Click a file in the file browser on the left. Choose the folder it shows with File > Open folder… or Open Unity project… (File browser).
Dropping on the window Drop files from Explorer or Finder outside the canvas (file list, start screen, tab strip, panels) to open each in a new tab. Images dropped on the canvas become layers of the current document (Dropping images onto the canvas).
Explorer · Finder Double-click a .chickxel file (see below).
What each file type opens as
File Opens as
.chickxel, .gpixel That project.
PNG The project that made the PNG if there is one; otherwise the PNG is imported as a new project (Opening (importing) PNGs).
JPG, BMP, GIF, WebP, ICO, animated PNG A new document with one frame per image frame (Opening images, animations and videos).
Videos (MP4, WebM, MOV, …), AVIF, HEIC Read with ffmpeg into a new document. Videos first show the Import video window (Opening images, animations and videos).
Opening by double-clicking in Explorer or Finder
Double-click a saved .chickxel project file in Explorer (Windows) or Finder (macOS) to open it. Double-clicking a .chickxel-asset asset package imports the assets inside. This file association is registered as follows on each OS.
OS File association
Windows Registered once you run the new version of the app. Every start registers the current Chickxel.exe for your user account (no administrator rights needed), so if you move the exe, start it once again.
macOS Associated once Chickxel.app is in the Applications folder.
Linux No file associations yet. Open files with File > Open or by dropping them on the window.
If the app is already running, the file opens as a document tab in that window instead of a new window (or switches to its tab if it is already open).
If another app is set to open .chickxel files, right-click the file and choose Chickxel under Open with (Windows) or Open With (macOS).
Previews in Windows Explorer
In Windows Explorer's Medium icons, Large icons and Extra large icons views, a .chickxel file shows the project's first frame instead of the app icon. The picture is enlarged without blurring the pixels and centered, with the palette chick badge at the bottom right so you can tell it's a Chickxel file. The Small icons, List and Details views keep showing the app icon.
Explorer reads only the thumbnail.png stored inside the file on save (see File types and where they go). Files saved before this feature show the app icon; open them in Chickxel and save once to get the picture.
Like the file associations, the preview is registered for your user account automatically when Chickxel starts (no administrator rights needed). If you move the exe, it's set up again the next time you start it.
Files changed outside the app
When an open project file is changed by another program (a sync app, another Chickxel window, …), Chickxel notices and does the following.
Case What happens
The document you are viewing Asks whether to reload (warning that your edits will be lost if there are any). Choosing No keeps the document as is; saving afterwards overwrites the externally changed file. Autosave pauses while asking.
Another tab without unsaved edits The file is reread when you switch to that tab.
Another tab with unsaved edits Keeps the edits in memory and notes it in the status bar. Saving overwrites the externally changed file.

Saving an imported PNG
